title: Integration of Mott neurons and spintronic memories for event-driven spiking neural networks
source: Nature Nanotechnology
abstract: Spiking neural networks provide energy-efficient, event-driven computing, but separating volatile neuronal dynamics from non-volatile memory imposes costly signal transfer and conversion. Here we demonstrate a hybrid compute-and-store core that directly integrates thermally coupled vanadium dioxide Mott leaky integrate-and-fire neurons to spintronic memory. The neurons require no external resistive or capacitive elements for temporal integration and write their output spikes into either domain-wall racetracks or spin–orbit torque magnetic tunnel junctions without amplifiers or analogue-to-digital converters. In racetracks, spike number and amplitude are converted into domain-wall displacement, spatially preserving temporal histories and enabling up to six spikes per processing cycle. Distinct spike trains generated from encoded input patterns produce separable non-volatile states, demonstrating event-based processing and read-out. A network model parameterized by experimental leaky integrate-and-fire neuron dynamics achieves 96.3% accuracy on MNIST digit recognition. Functional coupling of a 500-nm leaky integrate-and-fire neuron to a 100-nm spin–orbit torque magnetic tunnel junction further establishes nanoscale compatibility. The demonstrated compute-and-store core consumes 51.9 nJ per spike-to-memory conversion, with sub-200-nm vanadium dioxide devices indicating operation near 200 pJ, offering a scalable route towards dense, low-power edge neuromorphic systems for real-time sensory processing.

title: Clinical landscape of cardiometabolic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
source: Nature
abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) has emerged as the predominant form of heart failure worldwide and is increasingly associated with obesity, type 2 diabetes and systemic cardiometabolic dysfunction. This cardiometabolic HFpEF entity can be conceptualized as a mechanistically defined endotype marked by endothelial dysfunction, metabolic inflexibility and maladaptive inter-organ signalling involving the liver, kidney, adipose tissue and skeletal muscle. The cardiometabolic endotype often corresponds to a clinically recognizable adiposity-related clinical phenotype. Despite the growing prevalence of cardiometabolic HFpEF, therapeutic progress has lagged. This is mostly because the classification structure used is based on a commonly over-interpreted biomarker—ejection fraction—although inadequate trial end points and a lack of mechanism-guided precision also have a role. Here we review the evolving epidemiology, mechanistic underpinnings and emerging therapeutic landscape of cardiometabolic HFpEF. We highlight limitations in current diagnostic criteria, the role of extracardiac drivers and the need for soft end points and systems-based modelling. Advances in '-omics', phenotyping and cross-disciplinary frameworks now offer a pathway towards mechanistically targeted interventions that could enable symptomatic control by modifying validated disease mechanisms that culminate in this syndrome.

title: Structural basis of RNA-guided DNA integration by type I CAST systems
source: Nature
abstract: CRISPR-associated transposases (CASTs) achieve site-specific DNA integration by combining the RNA-guided targeting action of a nuclease-deficient CRISPR–Cas system with the assembly of a Tn7-like transpososome complex1,2. Understanding the detailed mechanisms of this elaborate process is paramount to engineering CAST systems into programmable genetic tools3,4,5,6. Type I-F Pseudoalteromonas CAST (PseCAST) shows the highest activity in mammalian cells so far7 and has been adapted extensively through directed evolution8. However, its continued rational engineering requires addressing critical gaps in our understanding of transpososome assembly and activation9. Here we perform structural analyses using cryogenic electron microscopy, validated by DNA transposition assays, to visualize the PseCAST system in a series of functional states that define the stepwise mechanism of RNA-guided DNA integration. The structures of the PseCAST targeting and transposase recruitment complexes revealed that conformational changes in the Cascade–TniQ module, induced by R-loop formation, are associated with target-DNA stabilization and TnsC heptamerization. This, in turn, results in the recruitment of the TnsAB transposase by conserved interactions with the carboxy-terminal tail of TnsB. Finally, the structure of the 1.2 MDa PseCAST transpososome holocomplex revealed allosteric coupling of TnsC–TnsB and TnsB–target-DNA interactions to the conformational remodelling of the TnsB catalytic site, activating donor-DNA integration. Together, these findings establish a unified mechanistic blueprint for RNA-guided DNA integration by type I CASTs and provide a structural framework to guide their engineering for genome-editing applications.

title: Transcription from megabase-scale heterochromatin generates neural barcodes
source: Nature
abstract: Heterochromatin typically represses genes1,2, yet some genes paradoxically require it for activation3,4,5,6,7. How can the same chromatin environment both silence and promote transcription? Here we address this question by interrogating the clustered protocadherin (Pcdh) locus, where subsets of genes are stochastically expressed while most remain silent8. In neurons, stochastic and combinatorial expression of Pcdh genes generates unique cell-surface barcodes required for self–non-self discrimination and neural circuit assembly8. By combining RNA labelling of Pcdh genes and neurodevelopmental cell types with single-molecule chromatin tracing and stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy, we find that a compact heterochromatin domain containing Pcdh genes forms as these genes become activated during development. Pcdh transcription occurs within the compact domain and reads through downstream genes, and distal enhancers must access the domain to engage target promoters. Genetic perturbations in mice suggest that opposing genome folding forces cooperate to establish Pcdh locus architecture and promote stochastic Pcdh expression. Specifically, while DNA loop extrusion allows enhancers to breach heterochromatin and find target promoters, heterochromatin-driven compartmentalization supports an expanded enhancer–promoter search space. These findings shed light on a process foundational to the development of vertebrate nervous systems and suggest a mechanism for how transcription can occur within seemingly silent chromatin environments.

title: Coherent parity oscillations in coupled minimal Kitaev chains
source: Nature
abstract: Majorana zero modes provide a route to fault-tolerant qubits by encoding information non-locally in fermion parity. Their noise sensitivity is expected to decrease exponentially with separation between Majorana zero modes, a suppression known as topological protection1. Kitaev chains in quantum-dot–superconductor arrays can host Majorana zero modes at their ends1,2, even in two-site chains3. These minimal-chain modes, known as poor man’s Majoranas, retain characteristic Majorana properties, including near-zero energy and equal electron–hole character, but lack topological protection3,4,5. A key challenge is moving from identifying these modes in electrical transport to coherent qubit control. Here we demonstrate coherent time-resolved rotations between parity states encoded by four poor man’s Majoranas in two coupled minimal Kitaev chains3,6,7,8. Total fermion parity conservation separates the system into global even- and odd-parity manifolds. We observe coherent parity oscillations in both, with frequencies matching within 5% at the poor man’s Majorana sweet spot, consistent with largely isolated Majoranas6. The oscillation frequency, rotation axis and coherence depend systematically on inter-chain coupling and quantum-dot detunings, in agreement with our model for short chains. Our results establish coherent control of a qubit encoded in the fermion parity of Majorana zero modes, realized using minimal Kitaev chains. They lay the groundwork for universal qubit operations, comprehensive coherence characterization and probing protection in longer chains.

title: Enzymatic living polymerization for polysaccharide synthesis
source: Nature
abstract: Polysaccharides have myriad functions throughout biological processes, yet synthetic access to well-defined analogues remains a challenge1,2. Achieving high molecular weight, controlled stereochemistry and sequence precision simultaneously has been elusive using conventional chemical methods that rely on protecting-group manipulations. Here we propose enzymatic living polymerization, which enables the precision preparation of natural polysaccharides with molecular weights up to 660 kg mol−1 but polydispersity from low to less than 1.05. Such a living behaviour originates from the initiator weakly binding with the polymerase, realizing fast equilibrium of the active (bound) and dormant (unbound) species, as demonstrated by mechanistic and computational studies. Our approach is generalizable to diverse polysaccharide types, including sequence-controlled block copolymers, and provides a modular route to explore molecular-weight-dependent biological functions of natural polysaccharides.

title: Augmenting reality with integrated photonics
source: Nature
abstract: Augmented-reality (AR) glasses promise to transform how we interact with the world by seamlessly blending digital content with our physical surroundings. Yet making them viable for comfortable, all-day use remains deeply challenging, constrained by hard trade-offs of size, power and display performance. This calls for fundamentally new ways to generate and control light with high precision in an ultracompact form factor. Here we examine how integrated photonics can help bridge the technology gap in AR hardware. We review the basics of AR displays and recent advances in integrated photonics for new AR display components and architectures, then turn to key challenges and future directions, from component development to system innovation and scalable manufacturing, and highlight broader opportunities for synergy with fields such as quantum computing, bioimaging and optical sensing.

title: Context-dependent response of endothelial cells to PIK3CA mutation
source: Nature
abstract: Cancer-associated mutations in PIK3CA underlie congenital overgrowth disorders that frequently involve the vasculature1,2. Among the affected tissues, the endothelium commonly exhibits aberrant expansion, leading to vascular malformations3. Notably, these lesions arise predominantly in veins and capillaries, whereas arteries are largely spared, for reasons that remain unclear. Here, using genetic lineage tracing, we show that endothelial expression of PIK3CAH1047R drives profound clonal expansion of capillary and venous endothelial cells, whereas mature arterial endothelial cells are refractory to pathological PI3K activation. Expression of PIK3CAH1047R in arterial precursors disrupts arterial differentiation and promotes the acquisition of venous features, providing a mechanistic explanation for the paucity of arterial lesions after PIK3CA genetic perturbation. Mechanistically, these effects are mediated by two complementary downstream branches of PI3K signalling: increased proliferation, which drives vascular overgrowth, and upregulation of the venous-specifying transcription factor NR2F2 (also known as COUP-TFII), which suppresses arterial differentiation. Together, our findings reveal that pathogenic responses to PIK3CAH1047R are dictated by endothelial differentiation state and fate trajectory, and demonstrate that arterial endothelium is intrinsically resistant to oncogenic PI3K signalling. Arteries are therefore shielded from PIK3CA mutations, explaining the rarity of arterial malformations in PIK3CA-driven disease.

title: Sustainable cement production via a liquid-phase pathway
source: Nature
abstract: Slowing climate change requires overcoming inertia in political, technological and geophysical systems1,2,3. Portland cement manufacturing is among the most challenging industrial processes to decarbonize, yet it remains indispensable for building the infrastructure underpinning the low-carbon transition4,5. Here, building beyond the two-century-old conventional cement process6, we report a route that creates sustainable cement, by accelerating its reaction kinetics through a microwave carbon-plasma method, reducing the standard processing time from hours to seconds. Our technique generates localized temperatures up to 2,400 °C, sufficient to liquefy the raw materials. These liquid-phase reactions promote elemental mixing and solidification, producing reactive clinker phases. Our in situ transmission electron microscopy captures the early-stage cement hydration process in real time, revealing that surface disorder accelerates clinker reactivity by facilitating the dynamic nucleation and growth of hydration clusters. Beyond typical limestone and clay feedstocks, we show that hydrated cement paste from waste concrete can also be processed into clinkers, meeting ordinary Portland cement specifications. By coupling circular resource use with ultrafast electrified processing, our approach enables sustainable, low-cost cement production at scale.

title: Middle–Late Pleistocene Denisovans and unresolved Homo in southern China
source: Nature
abstract: Molecular and morphological evidence increasingly supports the view that most East Asian Middle to Late Pleistocene archaic Homo belong to Denisovans1, yet the presence of other contemporaneous lineages has remained unclear. Here we report a set of newly discovered hominin fossils (4 isolated teeth; more than 100.8 thousand years ago and 104.5–42.6 thousand years ago, respectively) from 2 cave sites (Chuanshandong and Longchuandong) in Guangxi, southern China. Integrated morphological and palaeoproteomic analyses reveal substantial phenotypic and molecular diversity consistent with at least two distinct lineages. One lineage (Longchuandong) is assigned to a Denisovan-affinity population, owing to its extreme similarity to Altai Denisovans with respect to dental morphology and single amino acid polymorphisms that match those of Denisovans from Harbin, Penghu, Bianfu Cave and Altai. The other lineage, represented by the Chuanshandong hominin, is an unresolved archaic Homo, as it carries an ancestral variant (AMELY 179M) shared with Homo antecessor and great apes and another variant (AMBN 253G) that is diagnostic of East Asian Middle Pleistocene Homo erectus but lacks the Denisovan-associated AMBN 273V variant (it being highly probable that this is inherited from H. erectus). Dental morphology in this lineage exhibits a mosaic of plesiomorphic and derived traits but no clear Denisovan affinity. These findings indicate that diverse hominin populations may have inhabited subtropical China during the Middle and Late Pleistocene, including a Denisovan-affinity population and another unresolved archaic Homo.

title: An extremophile transgene improves drought resistance and yield in cereals
source: Nature
abstract: Drought is a major environmental constraint limiting global crop production1,2. On average, crop productivity typically declines by 30–40% in moderate-drought years, whereas extreme droughts trigger far greater reductions3,4. As droughts become longer and more intense due to climate change, adverse effects on crop productivity are expected to escalate5. Breaking the trade-offs between stress resistance and yield is key to advancing crop genetic improvement as climate change sets in and the world population grows, but this is challenging for drought stress6. Here we show that heterologous expression of EpTFIIAγ, a gene encoding a transcription factor induced by osmotic stress in an extremophile lichen mycobiont, partially decouples trade-offs between stress resistance and grain production, enhancing plot yields of five wheat cultivars under water deficit by 19.4–32.8%, and per-plant yields of rice and maize by 19.7–42.4% in the greenhouse and multiple field environments. EpTFIIAγ physically interacts with endogenous transcriptional activators to synergistically enhance both stress-responsive and developmental transcriptional programs, simultaneously boosting photosynthetic capacity and water-use efficiency, while delaying senescence via multiple physiological and developmental enhancements, ultimately increasing grain yields. EpTFIIAγ uncouples antagonistic stress-response and biomass production pathways in multiple crops and delivers a straightforwards and broad-spectrum strategy for sustainably improving staple-crop yields regardless of water availability.

title: Licensing mechanisms during RNA-guided DNA integration by type I-F3 CAST
source: Nature
abstract: Precise genomic integration of large DNA cargo remains a central challenge in genome engineering. CRISPR-associated transposases (CASTs)1,2 offer a promising solution by coupling RNA-guided DNA recognition to transposon-mediated integration. Because of their exceptional targeting fidelity, type I-F3 CASTs have been a major research focus1, yet the structural basis of their RNA-guided DNA integration has remained unclear. Here, using cryo-electron microscopy, computational protein design and functional assays, we report the licensing mechanisms that control DNA integration activity of Vibrio cholerae CAST (VchCAST). Structural determination was enabled by zero-shot computational redesign of TnsA, which enhanced integration activity by nearly two orders of magnitude without compromising specificity. The structure of the holo integration complex reveals the conformational licensing events that govern activation of the integration machinery at the on-target site. Multiple components (Cascade–TniQ, TnsC and TnsA–TnsB) undergo conformational changes upon assembly into the holo integration complex, and the catalytically competent state is stabilized only within the full assembly. Comparison with existing CAST integration complex structures reveals conserved architectural features, suggesting a common molecular basis for RNA-guided transposition across CASTs. Our findings establish a general mechanistic framework for RNA-guided DNA integration and demonstrate that protein design is a powerful strategy for engineering highly active CAST systems.

title: A gut–brain sensory-motor circuit regulates sugar ingestion in Drosophila
source: Nature
abstract: Bidirectional communication between the brain and digestive tract is critical for optimizing nutrient preference and food intake, yet the neural mechanisms that couple gut nutrient sensing with ingestive motor control remain poorly understood. Here we identify a gut–brain sensory-motor circuit that regulates sugar ingestion in flies. We show that the brain neurons that regulate food ingestion, IN1s1, receive excitatory input from enteric sensory neurons that penetrate the foregut epithelium and detect sugars in the gut lumen during ingestion. Functional imaging and connectome analyses reveal that IN1s integrate excitatory input from multiple sugar-sensing neurons, including enteric sensory neurons, and provide inhibitory output to enteric motor neurons that control the muscles at the entry of the crop—a stomach-like organ. During ingestion, IN1 activation suppresses these enteric motor neurons, relaxes the crop duct and promotes rapid transfer of food into the crop, thereby enabling sustained food intake. Together, our findings describe a gut–brain circuit that controls the motor activity of digestive tract muscles during feeding and suggest a circuit mechanism by which nutrient signals from the gut contribute to the dynamic regulation of food intake across metabolic states.

title: Heterogeneity co-evolves with architecture to determine colon cancer outcome
source: Nature
abstract: Intratumoural heterogeneity, originating from genetic, epigenetic and phenotypic diversity, is pervasive in cancer and a fundamental barrier to curative treatment1,2. How these heterogeneous cell states emerge and co-evolve within tumours remains poorly understood. Here we develop a deep-learning framework that quantifies colorectal cancer tissue architecture and nuclear morphology at subcellular resolution to predict patient outcome. Integrating this with spatial transcriptomics, multiplex immunofluorescence and patient-derived organoids, we identify a co-evolutionary relationship between tumour architecture and cancer cell states. We identify architectural interfaces in colorectal cancer that drive cell state diversification by promoting distinct cancer stem cell programmes. Specifically, tissue fragmentation generates compressive forces that activate YAP, suppressing classical stem cell programmes and inducing fetal/regenerative stem cell states that initially manifest as hybrid states with features of partial epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Subsequent tumour–stroma communication through TGFβ diversifies these into distinct stem cell and EMT states. Reciprocally, β-catenin activity tunes tumour cell responsiveness to architectural cues. Collectively, this work identifies a feedforward loop between cell states and tissue architecture that drives cancer heterogeneity and cell state diversification. Machine-learning-based analyses harness this co-dependency, independently of mutational status or cancer stage, to predict patient outcome.

title: Single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map for coronary artery disease
source: Nature
abstract: Although coronary artery disease (CAD) genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified hundreds of loci, most variants lie in non-coding regions, obscuring the causal gene programmes and cell types driving disease1,2. Here we performed single-nucleus multi-omic profiling of gene expression and chromatin accessibility in human coronary arteries from 44 people to construct a genome-wide single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map. We identified 11,269 chromatin accessibility quantitative trait loci (caQTLs) across principal vascular cell types, including CAD-associated caQTLs in smooth muscle cells (SMCs). Using dynamic single-cell caQTL modelling3, we show that variant effects on chromatin vary across SMC states. For example, rs658956-mediated suppression of the FGGY-DT enhancer through disruption of an AP-1 motif is amplified as SMCs transition towards a fibromyocyte fate. We next performed genome-wide high-throughput chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C) in 15 human coronary arteries, showing that rs4887091 in the ADAMTS7 CAD locus has allele-dependent effects on CCCTC-binding factor occupancy and loop strength. Integrating Hi-C, Hi-C with chromatin immunoprecipitation and in vitro clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats interference (CRISPRi) nominated AMOTL2 as a distal SMC-specific CAD gene whose loss promotes proliferation and suppresses contractile identity. Finally, arrayed Perturb–seq of GWAS-nominated enhancers converged on extracellular matrix remodelling as a core SMC disease programme. Together, these findings provide a framework for mapping non-coding GWAS variants to cell types, chromatin states and gene programmes in human disease.

title: An enduring climatic burden from past peatland drainage
source: Nature
abstract: Over millennia, peatlands have removed hundreds of gigatonnes of carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere but emitted a proportion back as methane (CH4), exerting a slow net cooling effect1. Artificial drainage of these ecosystems—a centuries-old practice2,3—causes decomposition and the re-release of CO2 but suppresses CH4 emissions4, with a net climatic effect that is not well quantified at the global scale5. Here we reconstructed the radiative forcing from worldwide peatland drainage over 1800–2020 by combining a new flux dataset, hydrologically driven models of CO2 and CH4 fluxes and a hindcast of drainage extent and intensity. We found that drainage has produced a net heating effect of +73 (48–99) mW m−2—equivalent to 2.7 (1.8–3.6)% of industrial-era radiative forcing—originating from 0.4–0.5% of global land area. The net heating results from the dominant forcing of drainage-induced CO2 emissions (+83 (52–110) mW m−2) over that of avoided CH4 emissions (−9 (−15–−2) mW m−2). Even without further expansion of drainage, maintaining currently drained areas could almost double the cumulative warming by 2100. Our reconstruction captures the opposing impacts of peatland drainage on global budgets of CO2 and CH4 and quantifies the strong legacy effects of historical drainage on present and possibly future climate.

title: Bogong moths can migrate using an internal geomagnetic compass
source: Nature
abstract: Australian migratory moths navigate long distances, in part owing to a stellar ‘compass’. It transpires that they have another compass that detects the inclination, or angle, of Earth’s magnetic field lines and that probably relies on a light-dependent quantum-mechanical mechanism similar to the one found in night-migratory songbirds. Migratory moths distinguish poleward from equatorward by sensing the inclination of magnetic field lines.

title: A fine-grained reconstruction of barley’s evolutionary history
source: Nature
abstract: Chromosome-scale genome sequences from across the barley genus Hordeum reveal large structural variation, evidence of ancient genetic exchange and extensive divergence of regulatory sequences. These evolutionary processes have generated diversity that could be used to improve cultivated barley. Genome sequences across Hordeum reveal conserved chromosome ends and coding genes, but divergent chromosome centres and regulatory DNA.

title: An in situ redox-converted molecule for all-perovskite tandem solar cells
source: Nature
abstract: All-perovskite tandem solar cells (TSCs) are gaining prominence due to their ability to surpass the efficiency limit of single-junction perovskite solar cells (PSCs)1,2. However, the efficiency and stability of all-perovskite TSCs are limited by chemical instability at the hole transport layer/perovskite interface in the tin-lead (Sn-Pb) narrow-bandgap subcell, which introduces deep trap states from tin cations and promotes non-radiative recombination3-5. Here we incorporate a redox-converted molecule of p-aminobenzohydrazide (ABH) into poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):polystyrene sulfonate (PEDOT:PSS) that neutralizes PSS acidity, heals Sn4+ defects, and generates a dipole passivation effect upon oxidation. During the preparation of Sn-Pb perovskites, ABH suppresses interfacial oxidation by reducing Sn4+ defects and converts to p-aminobenzaldehyde (ABD), which suppresses photogenerated hole-induced Sn2+ oxidation, aligning energy levels for efficient hole extraction. The in situ redox-converted molecule stabilizes the buried interface during both device fabrication and operation, reduces non-radiative recombination and enhances stability. The resulting narrow-bandgap Sn-Pb PSC achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.4% (certified 25.2%) with an open-circuit voltage of 0.92 V and a fill factor of 83.4%. Integrated into monolithic all-perovskite TSCs, the device delivers a PCE of 31.1% (certified 30.8%) together with enhanced thermal (ISOS-D-2I, 85 °C) and operational stability (ISOS-L-1I) under inert conditions.

title: Bioorthogonal catalytic materials for precise chemical control in living systems
source: Chemical Society Reviews advanceAccess
abstract: Bioorthogonal catalytic materials integrate diverse reactions, material designs, and responsive regulation for precise chemical control in living systems. Their versatility enables applications in protein engineering, diagnosis and therapy.

title: Quantum-enhanced sensing with 500 photons via Fock-space confocal focusing
source: Nature
abstract: Quantum metrology promises measurement precision beyond classical limits by exploiting large-scale quantum states1,2,3,4,5,6,7, yet realizing this advantage faces two fundamental challenges: the deterministic preparation of non-trivial quantum probes8,9 and the efficient extraction of metrological information in high-dimensional Hilbert spaces10,11,12. Here, we introduce quantum confocal microscopy in Fock space that addresses these challenges for a Fock-like probe state with a tightly concentrated photon-number distribution. Drawing a direct analogy between classical wave optics and quantum state evolution in a bosonic mode13,14, we construct a confocal lens system with a quantum circuit of O(1)" role="presentation">O(1){\mathcal{O}}(1) operational depth, realizing a bidirectional transformation between a readily obtainable coherent state and this Fock-like probe state. Using a superconducting circuit quantum electrodynamics platform, we deterministically prepare focused probe states with mean photon numbers up to N = 500, achieving a 21.5 ± 1.1 dB reduction of the photon-number variance relative to a coherent state. Using the focused states for displacement sensing, we achieve a record metrological gain of 19.20 ± 0.20 dB beyond the standard quantum limit. This work establishes quantum confocal microscopy as a compact protocol that makes high-photon-number non-Gaussian Fock-like probes experimentally accessible and measurable, providing a viable route towards quantum-enhanced precision measurement, and is readily extendable to other bosonic platforms and high-dimensional quantum many-body systems.

title: Disturbances and climate drive tree elevational shifts
source: Nature
abstract: Climate change and disturbances are reshaping forest ecosystems worldwide1,2,3,4, yet their combined effects on species redistribution remain poorly understood. Here we analyse repeated measurements from 44,368 forest inventory plots spanning 1999–2025, with an average remeasurement interval of 10 years, to examine how climate and natural disturbances jointly influence the elevational redistribution of tree species across the western USA. We show that climate warming increased sapling abundance, whereas increasing drought frequency and recent natural disturbances (fire, insect outbreaks and disease) reduced tree abundance, particularly among adult trees. By contrast, legacy fire was associated with increased sapling abundance, with stronger positive responses in angiosperms than in gymnosperms. These influences were distributed unevenly across species’ elevational ranges: upper portions of species’ ranges generally experienced stronger warming, greater increases in drought frequency and more disturbance activity than lower portions, creating elevational asymmetries in stress and recovery. These elevational asymmetries were associated with more pronounced downslope shifts in basal area centres, probably reflecting disturbance effects on larger trees. By contrast, stem abundance centres showed more divergent shifts, consistent with sapling responses to both climate change and disturbance. Our findings reveal contrasting demographic responses to climate change and natural disturbances that shape the elevational redistribution of different species, with potential consequences for forest composition, resilience and long-term stability.

title: Unconventional resistivity reduction in NbP semimetal nanoribbons
source: Nature
abstract: Modern and future electronics harbour a key challenge: as conventional metal wires shrink to nanoscale dimensions, their resistivity increases sharply1 owing to surface and grain-boundary scattering. To circumvent this unwanted behaviour, here, we explore the fundamental limits of charge transport in topological semimetal niobium phosphide (NbP) nanoribbons down to approximately 6-nm widths, with industry-friendly top-down nanofabrication. The extracted NbP nanoribbon resistivity reaches 18 ± 4.1 μΩ cm at room temperature with an approximately 9-nm2 cross-sectional area, lower than that of conventional metals and semimetals with comparable size. The NbP nanoribbon resistivity decreases with decreasing width, unlike the classical behaviour of metals such as copper. This trend suggests a growing relative contribution of surface and edge states as the nanoribbon cross-section is reduced, despite a certain amount of disorder, including edge roughness. Our findings advance the understanding of size-dependent transport and scaling in this class of semimetals, offering a platform for nanoscale wires and interconnects in future nanoelectronics.

title: De novo design of high-potency dual-target therapeutic peptides with ORIDTP
source: Nature
abstract: Peptides capable of modulating two therapeutic targets offer opportunities for treating complex diseases1,2. However, the development of such peptides at both targets is challenging, limited primarily by low design success rates and weak bioactivity. Here we present ORIDTP, an artificial intelligence platform that integrates single-target knowledge transfer and dual-target reinforcement to enable the rational design of high-potency peptides. ORIDTP successfully designed dual-target co-agonists for the GLP-1R and glucagon receptor (GCGR, also known as GLR), six of which surpassed the strongest natural binders of each receptor in bioactivity. Notably, the lead peptide GA-Dual.R5.S3 induced substantial weight loss and glycaemic improvement in diet-induced obese mice, and exhibited pronounced antidiabetic effects in db/db mice, without inducing nausea or aversion. Furthermore, ORIDTP demonstrated generalizability through successful zero-shot design of dual-target co-inhibitors for structurally and mechanistically distinct immune checkpoints, PD-1 and CTLA-4. Out of 15 designed peptides, 8 blocked both checkpoint interactions and 3 further exhibited in vivo antitumour efficacy in human checkpoint knock-in tumour-bearing mice. The lead peptide IC-Dual.P3 achieved the strongest tumour growth suppression, reducing tumour volume by 94.2% relative to controls. Together, these findings establish ORIDTP as a powerful and generalizable platform for de novo dual-target peptide discovery.

title: Ultrafast cellulose nanocrystal production from diverse lignocellulosic biomass
source: Nature Sustainability
abstract: The production of cellulose nanocrystals conventionally relies on hazardous chemicals and energy-intensive purification, limiting their sustainable and scalable manufacture. Here we propose a hydrolytic quasi-solvent strategy that enables the rapid extraction of CNCs from microcrystalline cellulose within 15 min, and lignin-containing cellulose nanocrystals directly from untreated biomass within 1 h, with near-closed-loop solvent recycling. Composed entirely of the ionic liquids 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium hydrogen sulfate and 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium chloride, the quasi-solvent leverages synergistic ionic interactions to enhance cellulose accessibility, surface functionalization and crystallite dispersion. Meanwhile, the imidazolium cations facilitate lignin removal from raw biomass through localized π–π interactions. Life cycle assessment shows that the recyclable process substantially reduces environmental impacts relative to conventional sulfuric acid hydrolysis and 2,2,6,6-tetramethylpiperidine-1-oxyl-mediated oxidation, while lowering estimated production costs by 55% and 33%, respectively. By integrating rapid nanocellulose extraction, direct biomass processing and solvent circularity, the present strategy provides a scalable and economically viable route towards resource-efficient lignocellulosic biorefineries.

title: Superspreading droplets for scalable and green perovskite photovoltaics
source: Nature Sustainability
abstract: Transitioning perovskite solar cells from laboratory demonstrations to commercial production requires minimizing raw material waste while maximizing manufacturing throughput. Although drop-coating is a continuous, potentially waste-free manufacturing route, its sensitivity to substrate surfaces has limited its wider adoption. Here we describe an ink formulation containing driving solvents that amplify outward surface-tension gradients, forcing droplets to rapidly spread over a wide range of materials, including highly hydrophobic surfaces. This superspreading mechanism enables near-complete utilization of the precursor chemicals, while accelerating film-deposition rates by more than 30-fold. Fully drop-coated perovskite solar cells achieved a power conversion efficiency of 26.36% (certified 26.11%). The formulation also preserves the underlying crystallization pathway during scale-up, allowing direct translation to industrially relevant coating techniques. A large-area minimodule fabricated by blade-coating achieved an efficiency of 22.81% over a 54.8 cm2 aperture. By decoupling droplet spreading from substrate surface chemistry, this strategy provides a broadly applicable route to high-throughput, material-efficient perovskite film manufacturing and advances the scalable production of high-efficiency photovoltaics.

title: Observationally-constrained CMIP6 projections of a snow-free Northern Hemisphere
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Northern Hemisphere snow cover retreat poses substantial climate risks, but large uncertainties in Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) hinder accurate projections of future evolution. We develop a monthly emergent constraint based on historical warming trends, which strongly correlate with ablation-season (May–October) snow cover loss. This constraint reduces inter-model variance by 17.0–58.4% under different emission scenarios and rectifies raw CMIP6 snow-loss biases. Constrained projections reveal that under the higher-emission scenario (SSP5-8.5), winter snow cover retreats in arid regions from the 2030 s, and Arctic summers become snow-free by the 2040 s. By mid-century, mid-latitude spring and autumn snow cover disappears, with arid and semi-arid regions approaching year-round snow-free conditions and humid regions losing 1–4 months of seasonal snow cover. Under the most sustainable scenario (SSP1-2.6) snow disappearance is delayed by 7.1–34 years relative to SSP5-8.5 across vulnerable regions and months. Overall, our constraint narrows projection uncertainty by 0.95–11.91 years, delaying projected disappearance by 0.01–2.65 years in transitional months while advancing it by 0.51–4.15 years in midsummer, providing refined month-specific baselines for climate risk assessments.

title: Suppressing interfacial water reactivity with an Eu20-encapsulated giant polyoxoniobate for stable zinc anodes
source: Matter
abstract: A water-stable giant polyoxoniobate (1Eu), featuring an Eu20 cluster encapsulated within an Nb88 shell, is introduced as an electrolyte additive for aqueous zinc batteries. Its abundant nucleophilic oxygen sites reconstruct hydrogen-bond networks and regulate Zn2+ solvation, thereby suppressing interfacial water reactivity and promoting uniform Zn deposition for stable and reversible Zn anodes.

title: Molecular-level pre-mixing enables robust high-entropy coating for sodium-ion battery cathodes
source: Matter
abstract: Uniform high-entropy coatings are challenging to construct on sodium-ion layered cathodes because conventional solid-state and wet-chemical routes are intrinsically constrained in achieving multicomponent homogeneity. Here, molecular-level pre-mixing is enabled by a high-entropy Prussian blue analog serving as an “all-in-one” precursor. During reactive annealing, the precursor consumes residual surface alkalis while forming a homogeneous high-entropy interphase, thereby enhancing initial Coulombic efficiency, rate capability, cycling stability, and air stability.

title: Achieving reversible triphasic switching of dizwitterionic azobenzene for selective molecular recruitment
source: Matter
abstract: Photoresponsive dizwitterionic azobenzene achieves highly reversible triphasic switching among homogeneous solution, liquid-liquid phase separation of coacervate droplets, and ordered crystals. This solution-coacervate-crystal triphasic transition enables hierarchical enrichment and stepwise sorting of fluorescent dyes and biomacromolecules, paving the way for programmable artificial cell compartments and smart separation materials.

title: Dye-based fluorescent organic nanoparticles: from chemistry to biology
source: Chemical Society Reviews advanceAccess
abstract:
Dye-based fluorescent organic nanoparticles (
                    d
                    FONs) are highly versatile and tunable nanoplatforms for bioimaging. This review highlights recent advances, current challenges and future opportunities to move
                    d

title: Localization of micron-scale lithium polysulfide-rich phases causes anode heterogeneity in lean-electrolyte lithium–sulfur batteries
source: Joule
abstract: Kim et al. reveal that concentrated lithium polysulfides form micron-scale, salt-anion-deficient phases in lean-electrolyte lithium–sulfur batteries, promoting heterogeneous interphase formation and uneven lithium deposition. Fragmenting these phases with a lithium iodide additive improves anode uniformity and cycling stability, establishing spatial electrolyte heterogeneity as a key consideration for practical batteries.

title: Computer vision links electroplated lithium morphology to lithium metal battery performance
source: Matter
abstract: Morphology is critical to materials research, yet its analysis often relies on subjective, qualitative observations that are difficult to quantify. Using lithium metal as a model, this study combines large-area automated microscopy with computer vision to establish quantitative descriptors of metal deposits. These measurements enable objective comparisons of lithium growth in different electrolytes and a combined criterion for rapid electrolyte screening. More broadly, this framework offers a transferable route toward quantitative, reproducible morphology analysis across materials science.

title: Synergistic high negative pressure enables direct lithium crystallization from raw salt-lake brine
source: Energy & Environmental Science advanceAccess
abstract: Solar-driven separation–crystallization pump achieves direct lithium crystallization from raw salt-lake brine by synergistic evaporation negative pressure and capillary negative pressure.

title: Molar-mass- and sequence-defined vinyl macromolecules via iterative photoredox decarboxylative addition of α-substituted acrylates
source: Nature Chemistry
abstract: Free-radical polymerization of simple vinyl monomers enables mass production of widely used polymers, but typically affords products that are poorly defined in molecular size and monomer sequence. Despite advances in precision polymerization, chain growth remains probabilistic, precluding molar-mass- and sequence-defined macromolecules. Here we report photoredox decarboxylative addition of bulky α-substituted acrylates, which enables quantitative addition of single building blocks without oligomerization. The α-acyl radical generated upon acrylate addition is irreversibly deactivated by rapid electron transfer within the photocatalytic cycle. A C(sp3)-centred radical is regenerated only after conversion of the terminal ester into a carboxylic acid and subsequent photoredox decarboxylation. Iterative photoredox decarboxylative addition yields vinyl macromolecules comprising residues identical to the repeat units of conventional vinyl polymers, without inseparable oligomeric impurities. Aperiodic vinyl-residue sequences can be assembled rapidly in continuous-flow reactors, offering a route towards fully automated synthesis of synthetic macromolecules and exploration of their sequence-dependent functions.

title: Metal-meets-acid: catalysis for lignin depolymerization
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Lignin, the most abundant renewable aromatic biopolymer on Earth, represents a highly promising feedstock for sustainable chemicals and biofuels. However, the efficient catalytic depolymerization of lignin remains challenging due to its robust interunit linkages and the tendency of reactive intermediates to form irreversible condensates. Acid-metal bifunctional catalysis has emerged as an effective strategy to address these challenges, as the acid sites and metal sites promote bond cleavage while stabilizing intermediates to suppress recondensation. This review focuses on the cooperative mechanisms between acidic sites and metal catalysts during lignin valorization. We examine the specific catalytic functions of these dual active sites, discuss how their bifunctional catalysis enables efficient depolymerization, and summarize recent advances in catalyst design. In the end, we provide perspectives on tuning the spatial distribution and matching degree of dual active sites, offering potential directions for the future development of effective lignin conversion catalysts.

title: Climate warming amplifies metabolic imbalance across global lakes
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Lake metabolism remains a critical yet poorly constrained component of the global carbon cycle. Here we integrate satellite observations, climate reanalysis data, free-water measurements derived metabolic estimates and machine-learning approaches to quantify lake metabolism across more than 4000 lakes from 2003 to 2024. We show that global lakes are overwhelmingly net heterotrophic, with ecosystem respiration (ER) exceeding gross primary production (GPP) in approximately 95% of lakes, generating a global metabolic imbalance equivalent to ∼2 Pg C yr−1. Temperature is the dominant control on metabolic variability, and warming stimulates ER more strongly than GPP across most climatic regions. Consequently, climate warming is projected to intensify both the annual mean and intra-annual variability of GPP and ER, leading to an 11% more negative annual net ecosystem production by the end of this century (−2.03 to − 2.26 Pg C yr−1). These findings highlight lake metabolism as an important component of carbon-climate feedbacks.

title: Submillimetre hot-electron transport in manganese-doped quantum dot solids
source: Nature
abstract: Colloidal quantum dot solids are promising for photoconversion and photochemistry, but their performance is fundamentally limited by rapid hot-carrier cooling, low carrier mobility and short transport ranges1. Here we demonstrate a spin-exchange-driven phototransport regime in manganese-doped quantum dot films that enables the generation, long-range transport and regeneration of hot carriers. Ultrafast spin-exchange-mediated Auger upconversion promotes electrons into high-energy, delocalized states before phonon cooling2,3, establishing a transient high-mobility conduction channel. Crucially, spin-exchange interactions not only generate hot carriers but also enable their repeated re-excitation, thereby sustaining long-range drift. This mechanism yields room-temperature mobilities of about 150 cm2 V−1 s−1 and submillimetre drift lengths—far greater than those of conventional quantum dot solids and approaching values characteristic of crystalline semiconductors. Time-of-flight measurements confirm drift-dominated transport, with transit times scaling linearly with distance and inversely with electric field. These results establish a route to long-range energy transport in nanoscale materials and enable the use of hot carriers in photoconversion, photochemistry and transit-time-limited photodetection.

title: Rare-variant genetic architecture of height in over 1.4 million individuals
source: Nature
abstract: Highly heritable, polygenic and easily measured, adult height has long been the model trait in human genetics1,2. Although the landscape of height-associated common genetic variation has been studied extensively2, rare variation remains relatively unexplored1. Here, using rare protein-altering variants in a discovery set of 826,066 exomes, we identify 207 height-associated genes, 98% of which replicate in an additional 624,567 individuals. The rarest and most deleterious class of variation, singleton (frequency ACAN) to +11 cm (FBN1) per allele, 52× larger than the average effect of common height-associated variants and comparable to the 1% tails of a common variant polygenic score. Several genes (TET1, DTL and IGF2BP2) have effect sizes that are at least as large as established Mendelian height genes, yet lack documented stature or skeletal growth syndromes, particularly for genes associated with increased height. Our large-scale sequencing study elucidates the genetic architecture and allelic heterogeneity of rare variants in height, providing unique insights into their large effects—often similar to or larger than recognized Mendelian syndromes—and their impact on trait prediction, clinical evaluation, and discovery power to facilitate drug target prioritization.

title: Engineering signalling centres to trigger human trunk morphogenesis in vitro
source: Nature
abstract: Vertebrate trunk development is orchestrated by endogenous signalling centres that generate gradients of signals such as WNT and BMP to pattern cell fates and drive morphogenesis1,2,3,4,5,6,7. Whether these cues alone can reconstitute human trunk-like morphogenesis in vitro remains unknown. Here we present a synthetic embryology platform for high-throughput, spatiotemporal delivery of morphogen signals to epithelial cysts derived from human pluripotent stem cells. Transient WNT and BMP gradients are sufficient to drive the generation of axially elongating trunk-like structures that contain a central neural tube flanked by axial, paraxial, intermediate and lateral mesoderm. The geometry of the transient BMP signal exerts lasting control over mediolateral patterning and bilateral symmetry. Patterning and morphogenesis are sustained by neuromesodermal and lateral plate mesoderm progenitors induced by the initial cues, which act as endogenous signalling centres. Together, these findings define a minimal spatial code sufficient to reconstitute trunk-like morphogenesis in a human stem-cell-based model and establish a scalable platform for studying early human development and congenital disorders.

title: Excitonic electrically tunable metaatoms for visible light
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Phase-gradient metasurfaces shape optical wavefronts through arrays of optical nanoantennas acting as metaatoms. While dynamic tunability forms a major frontier in this area, direct electrical switching of metaatoms operating in the visible has remained challenging. Here, we present an exciton-based metaatom that is electrically tunable and operates in the visible. Its function originates from an excitonic absorption band of a dedoped conjugated polymer, which together with low background permittivity induces optical metallicity in the visible. This allows anisotropic nanostructures to exhibit polarization-dependent optical response through localized surface exciton-polariton resonances, rather than plasmons or dielectric Mie resonances. This function can be fully switched off through reversible doping by small bias potentials, which turns off the exciton-induced metallicity. Our study details the mechanism of these metaatoms and demonstrates their use in electrically tunable phase-gradient metasurfaces for visible light, including erasable and rewritable holograms. This work thereby establishes a class of electrically switchable exciton-based metaatoms and expands the design space of dynamic visible metaoptics.

title: Stereoelectronic effects in glycan conformation
source: Chemical Society Reviews advanceAccess
abstract: This Tutorial Review discusses the stereoelectronic effects that determine glycan conformation. Chemical strategies to tune these effects and control glycan conformations are discussed to inspire new glycan designs.

title: Dynamic Oxygen Spillover–Structure Feedback in Asymmetric Site Catalysts: Stability Regimes and Design Principles
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Oxygen spillover refers to the transfer of oxygen‐containing species, including adsorbed intermediates and lattice‐derived oxygen, from a donor site/domain to a functionally nonequivalent acceptor through interfacial or connected surface pathways. Despite extensive studies of surface‐confined spillover, its atomic‐scale dynamics in asymmetric multi‐site catalysts remain elusive. This minireview summarizes forward, reverse, and cross‐site oxygen spillover and the key factors regulating these processes. These factors are categorized into intrinsic material properties, including composition, coordination and interfacial structures, and extrinsic operating conditions, such as applied potentials and local electrolyte environments. Moreover, we elaborate on how integrating in situ/operando spectroscopy with theoretical calculations elucidates the structure–activity relationships and dynamic structural evolution at elevated current densities. In particular, drawing on these mechanistic insights, we discuss rational design strategies for asymmetric multi‐atom site catalysts. Specifically, we emphasize how interface engineering, defect control, and self‐optimization methods promote the synergy of spillover effect and structural stability. Finally, we outline the future research direction and emphasize the urgent need to achieve higher space–time resolution in situ characterization and scalable synthesis of uniform asymmetric site catalysts for practical applications.

title: A Novel Metal‐Hydrogen‐Bonded Organic Framework (M‐HOF) Cathode Material for High‐Performance Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Lithium–sulfur (Li–S) batteries (LSBs) are highly promising for next‐generation energy storage devices, yet their practical application is hindered by severe polysulfide shuttling and sluggish sulfur conversion kinetics. Herein, a novel metal‐containing hydrogen‐bonded organic framework (HOF‐21) is constructed and integrated with carbon nanotubes and sulfur as cathode for Li–S batteries. The synergistic combination of hydrogen‐bonding networks and Cu coordination sites enables strong polysulfide anchoring and accelerates sulfur redox conversion. Experimental characterizations and theoretical calculations reveal that the unique framework structure containing metals and rich abundant hydrogen bonds effectively immobilizes soluble lithium polysulfides, while Cu active centers induce interfacial electronic coupling and optimize the thermodynamic conversion pathway of sulfur species. Benefiting from the adsorption–catalysis synergistic regulation, the HOF‐21/CNT@S cathode exhibits enhanced reaction kinetics, suppressed polysulfide migration, and improved interfacial stability. As a result, the assembled HOF‐21/CNT@S battery delivers excellent long‐term cycling stability with a capacity decay rate of only 0.06% per cycle over 500 cycles at 2 C at room temperature. Moreover, it maintains outstanding low‐temperature adaptability, achieving 76.8% capacity retention after 200 cycles at −10°C and 90.6% retention after 200 cycles at −20°C. This work provides a promising strategy for designing advanced cathode materials toward high‐energy‐density Li–S batteries.

However, currently reported CBPV predominantly focuses on lead‐containing hybrid perovskite ferroelectrics and the resultant CPL detectors are generally based on bulk crystals, hindering further applications of those materials. title: Stress‐Modulated Ionic Transport Limits Composite Cathode Kinetics in Solid‐State Batteries
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  High‐energy all‐solid‐state batteries (ASSBs) require thick composite cathodes, yet these architectures exhibit heterogeneous reaction distributions that limit their performance. Here, we show that chemo‐mechanical transport switching governs the spatiotemporal lithiation behavior of such electrodes. By combining operando depth‐resolved diffraction with microstructure‐resolved and multi‐scale simulations, we link utilization gradients to the dominant transport pathway and demonstrate that the reversal of reaction fronts between charge and discharge arises from dynamically evolving transport limitations. This switching originates from the coupled reconfiguration of electronic and ionic transport networks during cycling. Particle breathing and interfacial delamination disrupt electronic percolation, whereas the contact‐mechanics model indicates that stress‐field interactions within the solid electrolyte (SE) can limit ionic transport. The model predicts that this suppression depends on the activation volume and elastic properties of the electrolyte and can exceed an order of magnitude as interparticle spacing decreases at high active‐material loadings. Our findings establish a direct link between chemo‐mechanical evolution and transport control in solid‐state cathodes, and highlight the need for SEs with low pressure sensitivity and sufficient mechanical compliance to enable high‐energy ASSB architectures.

title: Photothermal Upcycling of Waste Polyolefins to Ethylene and Propylene Over Waste Plastic‐Derived Carbon Catalysts
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The efficient valorization of polyolefin wastes is challenged by the inertness of C─C bonds and the poor selectivity for olefins, which severely limits the conversion efficiency under mild conditions. Herein, a “treating waste with waste” strategy is proposed by using polypropylene waste derived carbon nanospheres (PP‐C) as the photothermal catalyst for polyethylene (PE) upgrading under focused Xenon light irradiation. Comprehensive characterizations identify that sp
                    2
                    ‐C domains with abundant edge defects of PP‐C serve as the catalytic active sites, which enable outstanding photothermal conversion and facilitate photogenerated charge separation. Theoretical calculations reveal that zigzag edges of sp
                    2
                    ‐structured graphene suppress the recombination of photogenerated charge carriers, thereby the localized electrons at the edge sites effectively weakens C─C bonds on the absorbed reactant and improves the photothermal catalytic efficiency. A remarkable olefin yield of ~60% with approximately 100% PE conversion is achieved within 10 min using PP‐C catalyst under sunlight condition, demonstrating great potential for practical applications. This work not only establishes a sustainable route for plastic valorization but also actively advances an innovative concept for the focused‐sunlight‐drives upgrading of polyolefins.

title: Sulfur Substitution of Oxygen‐Induced Multiferroic Phase Transition in Chiral Supramolecular Crystals
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Multiferroics exhibiting multiple ferroic orders have gained tremendous attention for decades owing to their intriguing properties and potential applications in future multifunctional devices. However, despite their unique advantages, such as inherent chirality—in contrast to traditional inorganic multiferroics, the design of molecular multiferroics with ferroelectricity and ferroelasticity remains a great challenge. Herein, through oxygen–sulfur (O/S) heavier congener substitution, we successfully designed the first chiral supramolecular ferroelectric–ferroelastic multiferroics [(
                    R
                    /
                    S
                    )‐1‐(2‐fluorophenyl)ethylamounium)(1‐thia‐15‐crown‐5)]BF
                    4
                    . We found that O/S substitution on parent chiral supramolecular compounds with no phase transition results in a 222F2‐type ferroelectric/ferroelastic multiferroic phase transition at 350 K, which can be attributed to the fact that the lower electronegativity of S than O weakens intermolecular interactions in the supramolecular system to reduce the energy barrier for molecular motions. Moreover, the O/S substitution induces remarkable chiral amplification, with the dissymmetry factor of the second‐harmonic generation circular dichroism (SHG‐CD) response one order of magnitude larger than that of the parent counterpart. Notably, such an SHG‐CD response can be switched from a high to a low state during the multiferroic phase transition. Our work opens up a new avenue for constructing multiferroic phase transitions in molecular systems and sheds light on the further exploration of chiral supramolecular multiferroics.
