We show that the scattering transform (ST), a wavelet convolution method, can extract geometric information from flow fields, offering insights beyond the power spectrum. The ST distinguishes balanced dynamics, internal waves, and different flavors of geophysical turbulence—even when their power spectra are identical. Applied to sea surface height (SSH) fields from ocean models, the ST differentiates regions with distinct underlying dynamics. Our analysis offers a framework for interpreting SSH from satellite altimetry and for analyzing other spatial maps (e.g., from airborne and coastal radar). More generally, the ST is an appealing way to characterize complex fluid motion in a variety of contexts.

title: Visual learning through auditory reactivation during wakefulness and sleep
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Visual learning, like other kinds of learning, has classically been attributed to intensive, active training; however, whether it can be achieved via effortless, passive reactivation remains unresolved. Here, we triggered targeted reactivation using auditory tones that had acquired contextual meaning through preceding visual–auditory associative learning. Re-exposure to learned tones improved subsequent visual performance during both wakefulness and slow-wave sleep. Wake reactivation matched training in both improvement and improvement per trial, whereas sleep reactivation surpassed both wake reactivation and training. By contrast, re-exposure to unlearned tones impaired performance only during slow-wave sleep. Reactivation-induced improvement and impairment were strictly orientation- and location-specific and were associated with a convergent auditory–visual coupling pathway. Beyond this shared pathway, auditory reactivation during wakefulness and sleep unfolded through distinct coupling architectures linking sensory and higher-order cortical regions. Collectively, our findings establish auditory reactivation as a highly efficient route to visual learning, identify sleep as its most potent state, and reveal a double-edged, state-dependent neuroplastic architecture.

title: Cryo-EM reveals a transmembrane allosteric site and activation mechanism for the SERCA calcium pump
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Impaired sarco-endoplasmic reticulum Ca
                    2+
                    -ATPase (SERCA) activity contributes to defective calcium handling and cellular dysfunction in cardiovascular and metabolic diseases, yet the structural basis of small-molecule SERCA activation has remained unknown. SERCA is a ubiquitous P-type ATPase that restores cytosolic Ca
                    2+
                    to the sarco-endoplasmic reticulum and is essential for cardiac Ca
                    2+
                    cycling and cellular energy homeostasis. Here, we used cryogenic electron microscopy to define how two chemically distinct activators, CDN1163 and UM-52, enhance SERCA function. Structures at 2.6 Å and 3.1 Å resolution show that both compounds bind the same previously unrecognized activation hotspot in the transmembrane domain, a shallow groove formed by helices M3 and M4 and capped by M1. Despite limited chemical similarity, both activators share conserved interactions with Ser265 and Trp272 and stimulate Ca
                    2+
                    -dependent ATPase activity. Activator binding promotes a catalytically competent, calcium-bound E1-like conformation of SERCA that may involve altered protein-lipid interactions. These findings establish a structural framework for rational design of potent next-generation SERCA activators.

title: Oligodendrocyte ER-phagy restricts excessive myelination by degrading sphingolipid synthases
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Myelination is critical for nervous system function. Numerous signaling pathways have been identified that promote myelin sheath growth, disruption of which can lead to hypomyelination. However, the negative regulators of myelin sheath expansion remain poorly defined. Here, we identify endoplasmic reticulum (ER)–phagy as a cellular brake on central nervous system myelination that restricts myelin sheath thickness during brain development. ER-phagy is active in oligodendrocytes during myelin membrane expansion and limits the abundance of ER-resident sphingolipid synthases, including ceramide synthase 2 (Cers2). Impairment of ER-phagy accumulates ER, elevates sphingolipid production, drives excessive myelin thickening, and alters social behavior after prolonged juvenile social isolation. Genetic deletion of Cers2, which synthesizes long-chain ceramides essential for sphingolipid biogenesis, rescues the hypermyelination phenotype caused by ER-phagy disruption. Together, our findings establish that ER-phagy–sphingolipid axis represses myelin growth and reveal a mechanistic link between ER homeostasis and myelin production by oligodendrocytes, providing insight into the cellular mechanisms underlying pathological hypermyelination.

title: A divergent bat orthopneumovirus with zoonotic potential constrained by RSV adaptive immunity and broad-spectrum treatment
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV; genus
                    Orthopneumovirus
                    ) causes severe pneumonia in young children worldwide, yet the zoonotic potential of the few known nonhuman animal orthopneumoviruses remains unknown. Here, we characterized a highly divergent bat orthopneumovirus (BPV) from West African straw-colored fruit bats and established a systematic framework for evaluating zoonotic risk posed by an emerging viral pathogen. Epidemiologic data in bats showed a low viral detection rate (24 of 1778 RT-PCR positive) and low seroprevalence (6 of 66 IgG IFA positive), suggesting BPV episodic circulation potentially sustained in immunologically naïve bats following bat birthing events. Near-complete genomes from two BPV genetic variants revealed prototypic orthopneumovirus organization, but lacked the
                    SH
                    viroporin-encoding gene present in RSV. Functional experiments showed that BPV NS1/NS2 antagonized human interferon β responses, and that BPV pseudoviruses entered human cells (4.5- to 53.5-fold less efficiently than RSV), while being cross-neutralized by human RSV-reactive antisera, together suggesting zoonotic traits that may be partly constrained by cross-protective immunity. BPV escaped neutralization by RSV-specific therapeutic palivizumab and inhibition by lonafarnib, but remained susceptible to MPE8, a broad-spectrum monoclonal antibody that targets the conserved pneumovirus antigenic site III. These findings identify zoonotic traits of a divergent bat pneumovirus while suggesting potential protective value of preexisting RSV immunity and broad-spectrum interventions, which has implications for pandemic preparedness. Whether cross-protection in the human population may change by the advent of RSV vaccination warrants investigation. Efforts to investigate orthopneumovirus host shifts, reservoir studies, and development of broadly reactive orthopneumovirus vaccines and antivirals are warranted.

title: The circSRSF5-FUS-EIF4A3 regulatory circuitry protects Ewing sarcoma cells from EWS::FLI1 small-molecule inhibition
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Circular RNAs (circRNAs) have become a key focus in cancer research due to their high stability, diversity, and ability to regulate various biological processes. This study explores the impact of small-molecule inhibition of EWS::FLI1 oncogene by YK-4-279 in Ewing sarcoma (ES). ES is a rare and highly aggressive childhood cancer driven by fusion proteins that disrupt normal gene regulation and promote tumor growth. Current treatments rely on intensive chemotherapy with serious long-term side effects, emphasizing the need for targeted therapies. A promising new approach targets the interaction between EWS::FLI1 and the RNA helicase DHX9 through the small molecule YK-4-279, which displays strong antitumor effects and has advanced to clinical trials. Transcriptome profiling revealed widespread changes in circRNA expression after YK-4-279 treatment, with a notable up-regulation of
                    circSRSF5
                    . Functional and mechanistic evidence identifies a key role for
                    circSRSF5
                    in tumor cell survival by stabilizing the anti-apoptotic protein eukaryotic translation initiation factor 4A3 (EIF4A3) and contributing to therapy resistance. These findings uncover a previously unidentified role for circRNAs, particularly
                    circSRSF5
                    , in ES pathogenesis and treatment response.

title: Stress unmasks disconnected endocrine coordination of glucose metabolism in Duchenne muscular dystrophy
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Skeletal muscle orchestrates systemic metabolism, dynamically coordinating glucose uptake and fuel use to match energy demand. In Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD), loss of dystrophin is associated with altered metabolic regulation. Using physiological stress to unmask metabolic deficits in the
                    mdx
                    mouse model of DMD, we show that stress hormone signaling rises without an appropriate poststress rise in insulin secretion, maintaining hyperglycemia despite elevated basal glucose uptake in skeletal muscle. Rather than reflecting increased gluconeogenesis, this hyperglycemia appears to stem from impaired glucose oxidative disposal; skeletal muscle stores glucose as glycogen instead of oxidizing it, while the heart and brain show persistent, tissue-specific uptake differences. Restoring insulin availability transiently corrects glucose control and reverses stress-induced deficits. Instead of correcting glucose handling, removing excess glucose directly using empagliflozin (SGLT2 inhibitor) prevents stress-induced increases in blood glucose. These findings identify a breakdown in endocrine-metabolic coordination underlying metabolic vulnerability in DMD and demonstrate two mechanistically distinct routes, restoring insulin secretion or bypassing it entirely, to restore metabolic resilience under stress.

title: Hardware-encoded modality separation for multimodal sensing and artificial perception
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Human skin achieves robust perception by distributing modality-specialized receptors that preferentially encode mechanical and thermal cues. Yet, soft and flexible tactile sensors often suffer from cross-sensitivity, where stretching, bending, and temperature variations generate overlapping electrical readouts that undermine reliable multimodal measurement and downstream artificial intelligence–based interpretation. Here, we present a multimodal piezoresistive platform based on doped silicon nanomembranes that leverages their crystallographic anisotropy and a bilayer differential architecture for front-end modality separation. By integrating [110] longitudinal/transverse gauges with [100] reference gauges that exhibit reduced piezoresistive sensitivity but comparable temperature coefficient of resistance, together with a bilayer differential layout, the platform compensates thermal drift and decouples stretching from bending at the hardware level. Experimental and theoretical analyses establish a quantitative framework for separating modality-specific responses under combined stretching, bending, and temperature stimuli. Integrated into a flexible, wireless platform, the decoupled signals enable real-time transmission and deep learning–based interpretation, allowing accurate identification of geometrically similar objects with distinct thermal or mechanical properties. These results highlight the feasibility and need to co-design front-end sensing architectures and learning models to achieve robust, high-accuracy multimodal decoupling in real-world conditions.

title: GDF15 impacts chronic kidney disease and associated weight loss through distinct mechanisms
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is frequently accompanied by anorexia, cachexia, and inflammation, which collectively contribute to poor clinical outcomes. However, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here we demonstrate a pivotal role for growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF15) in CKD morbidities. Deteriorating renal function and clinical disease status correlates with GDF15 levels in plasma and kidneys of CKD patients. In a mouse CKD model, GDF15 levels are elevated and
                    Gdf15
                    knockout (
                    Gdf15
                    −/−
                    ) mice are partially protected from CKD-induced anorexia and weight loss despite worsening renal function and inflammation. GDF15 receptor
                    Gfral
                    knockout (
                    Gfral
                    −/−
                    ) mice recapitulate these phenotypes. Metabolic cage studies reveal that the weight loss-protection effects are primarily attributed to increased food intake. Intriguingly, pair-fed
                    Gdf15
                    −/−
                    and
                    Gfral
                    −/−
                    mice exhibited phenotypic and molecular divergence. Pair feeding in
                    Gdf15
                    −/−
                    mice reverses loss-of-GDF15’s effect on body weight but does not restore renal functions. In contrast, pair feeding in
                    Gfral
                    −/−
                    mice reverses loss-of-GFRAL’s effect on both body weight and renal function. Transcriptome analysis suggests that GDF15 may act through both GFRAL-dependent mechanisms on food intake and GFRAL-independent mechanisms that primarily modulate inflammation and metabolic pathways. A monoclonal antibody that neutralizes circulating GDF15 markedly restores food intake and preserves body weight, demonstrating the therapeutic potential of targeting GDF15 in CKD-associated weight loss. Together, these findings demonstrate GDF15-GFRAL as a potential therapeutic target for CKD-associated weight loss and suggest GFRAL-dependent, food intake-mediated actions of GDF15 and food intake-independent effects that may contribute to renal inflammation and metabolic regulation.

title: Aclarubicin disrupts RNA polymerase II progression at replication-coupled histone genes
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Anthracyclines are effective chemotherapeutic agents that cause DNA and chromatin damage. One member of the anthracyclines, aclarubicin, has gained therapeutic interest due to its ability to kill cancer cells through chromatin-based mechanisms, thus avoiding the off-target effects associated with DNA damage. However, the molecular mechanism of action leading to aclarubicin-induced chromatin damage remains elusive. Here we performed Cleavage Under Targets and Tagmentation (CUT&Tag) of RNA polymerase II (Pol II) and other transcriptional regulators in human cells following aclarubicin treatment. We found that aclarubicin strongly disrupts the replication-coupled histone genes, resulting in a nonproductive accumulation of Pol II transcription machinery at levels exceeding those at other genes. We attribute this sensitivity to the dense Pol II loading and rapid transcription of the histone genes, which intensify the chromatin-disrupting effects of aclarubicin. Together, our findings shed light on the mechanism of aclarubicin as an anticancer drug and point to the replication-coupled histone genes as a target for therapeutic intervention.

title: Errors in social network knowledge predict how ties evolve in the future
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
A notable feature of people’s social knowledge is that it is riddled with errors. These errors, e.g., making mistakes about who are actually friends in a social network, has typically been attributed to cognitive limitations or heuristics that prioritize knowledge of general social patterns over details about specific ties. Here, we demonstrate that such errors instead reflect an adaptive link prediction process that anticipates how the network will evolve far into the future. By longitudinally following a large, real-world social network (
                    n
                     = 196) and tracking the formation and dissolution of social ties over the course of a year, we show that judgments that are wrong in the moment accurately forecast which relationships will emerge or dissolve up to 6 months later. On average, participants’ errors predicted tie formation nearly 3× and tie loss more than 1.2× above chance levels. Beyond the use of simple heuristics like triadic closure and homophily, computational modeling reveals that successful link prediction relies on mental representations of the social network that integrates information about both direct and indirect, long-range ties between individuals. Having a social network representation that is future-oriented yields distinct social advantages: Those who are better able to predict changes in the network become more centrally positioned over time, contingent on their initial position.

title: Probabilistic neural code for subjective value and metacognition in human cortex
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Subjective value underlies many everyday decisions, yet the neural representations supporting these valuations are inherently noisy and subject to uncertainty. Whether humans have metacognitive access to this uncertainty and how this access is supported neurally remain unclear. Here, we provide converging behavioral and neural evidence that subjective value is represented probabilistically in the human brain. Behaviorally, participants’ uncertainty reports tracked trial-by-trial fluctuations in valuation. Neurally, we decoded probability distributions over value from functional magnetic resonance imaging activity in ventromedial prefrontal and orbitofrontal cortex, and superior parietal lobe and intraparietal sulcus. Decoded neural uncertainty predicted behaviorally reported uncertainty across trial, item, and individual levels. Moreover, predicting behavioral uncertainty required modeling the covariance structure of population noise. These findings indicate that neural populations jointly encode value and uncertainty, extending probabilistic population coding from perception, working memory to subjective value, and providing a neural basis for metacognitive access to uncertainty in value-based decisions.

title: Ubiquitination of USP5 by a bacterial effector inhibits NLRP3 inflammasome activation
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
The intracellular pathogen
                    Legionella pneumophila
                    employs a repertoire of effector proteins to manipulate the host ubiquitin signaling and subvert host immune responses. In this study, we reported that the
                    L. pneumophila
                    effector GobX (Lpg2455) functions as a ubiquitin ligase to target the host deubiquitinase USP5. Ubiquitination of USP5 by GobX inhibits its deubiquitination activity. Furthermore, this ubiquitination enhances the interaction between USP5 and the host E3 ligase MARCHF7, thereby facilitating MARCHF7-dependent ubiquitination of NLRP3. This modification targets NLRP3 for autophagic degradation, ultimately suppressing NLRP3 inflammasome activation in macrophages. Our findings uncover a sophisticated strategy in which a bacterial effector hijacks the host ubiquitination machinery to dampen inflammasome signaling.

title: Uterine-derived anisotropic compressive force specifies the anterior-posterior axis orientation in the mouse embryo
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The establishment of the anterior-posterior (A-P) axis is a fundamental process in embryonic patterning. In mice, directional migration of the anterior visceral endoderm (AVE) determines the A-P axis, yet the cues directing migration remain elusive. Here, we show that anisotropic compression directs AVE migration toward the minor-axis end of the deformed embryo, using ex utero culture with controlled compression and in utero pharmacological manipulations of uterine mechanics. This compression induces localized accumulation of basement membrane (BM) components, including COLLAGEN IV, which directs the AVE toward the minor-axis end. Mathematical modeling demonstrates that BM density-dependent AVE-BM adhesion accounts for the observed AVE dynamics. Our findings reveal that the maternal mechanical environment provides directional cues for cell migration, bridging tissue-scale mechanics and biochemical patterning during body axis specification.

title: Historical evidence that wildfire frequency modulates debris-flow hazards through sediment-supply limitation
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Southern California is an epicenter of postwildfire debris flows. In this region, steep topography, frequent fire, heavy rainstorms, and large populations along the wildland-urban interface conspire to produce costly debris flows. Wildfire frequency in the region has tripled in recent decades, causing concern about escalating debris-flow hazards. Here, we investigate how wildfire frequency affects the magnitude of postfire erosion by analyzing long-term debris basin records. We identify two contrasting erosional styles. In steep catchments, erosion exhibits a binge-purge behavior: Erosion for 3 years following fire exceeds background rates by ∼17×. In contrast, in low-sloping, soil-mantled catchments, sediment export following fire only exceeds background rates by ∼1.5×. Critically, in the steep catchments, debris-flow volumes decline when wildfires recur more frequently than the ∼30-year interval characteristic of the past century. This observation suggests a sediment-supply limitation in which more frequent wildfire may reduce, rather than amplify, some of Southern California’s most severe debris-flow hazards.

title: Spaceflight reshapes Alzheimer’s disease–associated molecular programs in human brain organoids
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Spaceflight provides a unique environment to study neural responses relevant to neurodegenerative diseases. Here, human cortical organoids derived from induced pluripotent stem cells that carry familial Alzheimer’s disease (AD) mutations in APP,
                    PSEN1
                    , and
                    PSEN2
                    were cultivated at the International Space Station alongside Controls for 40 days. Multiomic profiling, integrating transcriptomics and proteomics, revealed a coordinated shift in neuronal and cellular states during spaceflight. Spaceflight was associated with changes in amyloid-β processing and tau phosphorylation, although the magnitude of these responses varied across genetic backgrounds. Pathway analysis identified increased synaptic and neurotransmission-related signatures, particularly those associated with GABA-releasing and glutamatergic signaling. Integrative analysis further revealed convergent programs involving RNA processing, chromatin organization, cytoskeletal dynamics, and cellular stress responses. Proteomic and multiomic analyses also identified changes in RNA binding proteins, including CIRBP, consistent with altered posttranscriptional regulatory networks under spaceflight conditions. These exploratory findings indicate that spaceflight reshapes neuronal regulation in human brain organoids, revealing coordinated molecular responses relevant to AD biology.

title: From genetic risk factor to therapeutic target: The CREB3L4-GDF15 axis drives prostate cancer immune evasion
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Advanced prostate cancer (PCa) is characterized by rapid progression and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, contributing to poor clinical outcomes and limited therapeutic responses. Mendelian randomization (MR) uses genetic variants as instrumental variables to assess causal associations while minimizing confounding and reverse causation. Through integrative proteogenomic analysis, including MR and colocalization across 438,178 males, we identified CREB3L4 as associated with PCa risk. CREB3L4 overexpression promoted tumor growth in mice, accompanied by activation of cholesterol metabolism, androgen receptor (AR) signaling, and immunosuppression. Single-cell RNA sequencing revealed CREB3L4 enrichment in human PCa cells. Interaction analysis identified enhanced growth and differentiation factor (GDF) signaling in CREB3L4
                    +
                    tumor cells, with CD8
                    +
                    T cells as the primary receivers. Ligand–receptor analysis and coculture experiments identified GDF15 as the key mediator, through which tumor cells suppressed CD8
                    +
                    T cell proliferation and activation via TGFBR2 signaling. In vivo, GDF15 neutralization attenuated CREB3L4-driven tumor growth and CD8
                    +
                    T cell dysfunction, whereas prostate-specific CREB3L4 knockout or adeno-associated virus-mediated knockdown suppressed tumor growth and restored CD8
                    +
                    T cell function. Clinical analyses confirmed elevated CREB3L4 and GDF15 expression in PCa, inversely associated with CD8
                    +
                    T cell infiltration and immunotherapy response. Collectively, these findings reveal that CREB3L4 promotes AR signaling-mediated GDF15 expression, driving CD8
                    +
                    T cell dysfunction and identifying the CREB3L4–GDF15 axis as a potential therapeutic target in PCa.

title: A precipitation threshold delineates contrasting controls on global soil pH under nitrogen fertilization
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Nitrogen fertilization is a major driver of soil acidification globally, yet its independent effects on soil pH and the underlying mechanisms remain poorly resolved. Here we isolate the contribution of nitrogen fertilization by compiling the largest paired experimental dataset to date, consisting of 3564 paired soil pH observations under control and nitrogen fertilization treatments across seven major ecosystem types worldwide. By constructing robust machine-learning models, we predict global soil pH under nitrogen fertilization (pH_T) and quantify fertilization-associated pH change under a standardized hypothetical fertilization scenario. Under this scenario, we estimate that 96.27% of global soils undergo acidification, with a mean pH decline of 0.34 units. Critically, we identify a precipitation threshold at ∼900 mm year
                    −1
                    that separates two distinct regimes in the relationship between precipitation and pH_T: climate-driven leaching and buffering in drier regions versus soil-mediated internal regulation in humid regions. This threshold demonstrates that the association between precipitation and pH_T is not uniform across the global precipitation gradient but varies markedly among hydroclimatic regions. Our results provide a global outlook on soil pH responses to nitrogen fertilization, supporting acidification risk early warning, precision fertilizer management, and sustainable agricultural development.

title: Arctic forcing of European spring productivity and agricultural yields linked to Barents Sea ice loss
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Arctic sea ice loss reshapes midlatitude climate, yet its cascading impacts on terrestrial carbon cycling and food security remain unclear. Barents Sea ice area (BSIA) has experienced the Arctic’s fastest decline. Using four decades of satellite observations, agricultural statistics, and Earth system model (ESM) simulations, we identify late-winter BSIA as a key driver of European spring productivity. Interannual BSIA reductions substantially enhance gross primary productivity (GPP) and raise national wheat yields by up to 16.5% in Eastern Europe, a global breadbasket. Reanalysis and model experiments reveal that reduced BSIA alters large-scale circulation through stratosphere-troposphere coupling, wave–mean flow interactions, and Rossby wave propagation. Anomalous subsidence drives adiabatic and radiative warming; cyclonic flow strengthens warm-air advection, together alleviating thermal constraints on photosynthesis. Although most ESMs capture atmospheric teleconnections, they systematically underestimate productivity responses due to underrepresented GPP-temperature sensitivity. BSIA decline accounts for approximately half of the four-decade increase in Eastern European productivity, highlighting an overlooked Arctic forcing of midlatitude carbon dynamics.

title: A flexible fiber–based artificial chemical postsynapse
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: Most artificial synapses, which are designed to communicate with biological neural systems and exhibit neuron-like functions, rely primarily on electrical signals. Biotic-abiotic neural interfaces that use artificial synapses to communicate with biological synapses via chemical neurotransmitters while exhibiting synaptic plasticity are of great interest. Here, we present an artificial chemical postsynapse that directly interfaces with biological systems through dopamine (DA) neurotransmitters and demonstrates synaptic plasticity–like behavior. The artificial postsynapse of a flexible fiber–based organic electrochemical transistor (F-OECT) with a capacitive-like charging gate electrode, which combines volumetric charge storage and DA-sensing functionalities, can detect pulsatile DA release and transduce these sensing signals with plasticity-like behavior. The F-OECT synapse emulates key synaptic functions observed in biological synapses by responding to pulse-like DA release from dopaminergic cells. We also implanted fiber-based artificial postsynapses into a mouse brain to study their basic interaction with DA release and to evaluate biocompatibility.

title: Signals of rapid genetic change in reef coral over time and following mass mortality
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Future coral reef persistence amidst accelerating climate change depends on rapid adaptive capacity. Sixteen years (2003 to 2019) of genetic data (
                    N
                     = 903) spanning mass mortality events uncovered polygenic signals of evolution and population structure in one Great Barrier Reef coral species (
                    Acropora tenuis
                    ) and a similar but nonsignificant trend in another (
                    Acropora millepora
                    ). Random forest revealed larger genetic shifts postbleaching compared to other time points, which was further supported by critical transitions in 34 years of remotely sensed thermal data (1985 to 2018). Concordant signals across multiple genomic ordinations confirmed significant shifts postbleaching. Specifically, three genetic variants contributed significantly to key random forest splits over time in
                    A. tenuis
                    . Significant genome-wide covariance in allele frequencies suggests shifts due to selection, not drift. This suggests that coral gene pools are changing, and measurable evolution can happen over subdecadal timescales, giving hope for coral resilience amid the ongoing climate crisis. However, we caution against overoptimism, and stress emissions must be urgently reduced.

title: Bioinspired mucolytic microrods for active mucus penetration and enhanced antibiotic delivery against H. pylori
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Helicobacter pylori
                    infects half of the global population and is a major driver of gastric cancer. Clinical eradication remains challenging because antibiotics must survive the acidic gastric lumen, penetrate the viscoelastic mucus barrier, and reach bacteria residing near the gastric epithelium. Here, we report a biomimetic oral delivery system that integrates rod-shaped morphology, acid protection, active mucolysis, and localized antibiotic delivery. The platform consists of clarithromycin-loaded Santa Barbara Amorphous-15 silica microrods coated with a pH-responsive alginate-pronase conjugate. The coating protects clarithromycin and pronase under acidic gastric conditions, while the less acidic inner mucus microenvironment promotes coating detachment and pronase-mediated mucolysis, enabling active mucus penetration. In vitro and in vivo studies show that these bacteria-mimicking microrods significantly enhance mucus penetration and increase gastric residence time twofold. In a murine infection model, the platform achieved 100% eradication at 15 milligrams per kilogram and maintained 90% clearance at 7.5 milligrams per kilogram, producing a ∼2000-fold bacterial burden reduction compared to free clarithromycin. This bioinspired, shape-guided strategy offers a promising paradigm for localized gastrointestinal therapy.

title: Tuning microswimmer motility by liposome encapsulation: A membrane clutch enables controlled swimming and cargo transport
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Inspired by biology’s use of vesicles for targeted transport, many studies have propelled liposomes with active matter, creating synthetic systems that can be viewed as microscale biohybrid robots. Nevertheless, the underlying motility mechanisms from a hydrodynamic perspective are often unresolved, and reliable velocity control remains challenging. In the present study, we use our previously introduced biohybrid system termed the chlamylipo, in which the motile alga
                    Chlamydomonas reinhardtii
                    is encapsulated within a giant liposome, as a model system to investigate how liposome encapsulation regulates microswimmer motility under controlled perturbations. From a fluid mechanical perspective, we establish a deformation-velocity expression that incorporates liposome radius, beating frequency, and membrane protrusion. We further show that motility can be reversibly switched by incorporating light-responsive lipids, with the liposome acting as a “clutch” that modulates membrane protrusion. To demonstrate its transport function, we further show cargo loading, carrying, and triggered release. These results show that liposome encapsulation can convert a motile microorganism into a controllable carrier, with the membrane acting as a clutch that regulates swimming and, therefore, cargo transport.

title: Atomic-scale visualization and assignment of contaminant adsorption geometries at mineral surfaces
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Directly resolving coexisting adsorption geometries at mineral-water interfaces and assigning them to crystallographic sites remains challenging in environmental geochemistry. Ensemble methods provide population-averaged structural constraints but may obscure minor or similar configurations and do not directly reveal crystallographic registry. Here, we establish an experimentally constrained framework integrating controlled off-axis high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM), multislice simulations, and density functional theory (DFT) to resolve crystallographic adsorption registries and corresponding structures. For selenium(IV) adsorption on hematite (001), comparison of apparent selenium positions with multislice simulations accounting for tilt-induced registry shifts supports assignment to iron-iron bridge and oxygen-centered hollow registries. DFT favors monodentate inner-sphere structures compatible with these registries. Extension to lead(II) and uranium(VI) on multiple hematite facets demonstrates the transferability of the off-axis imaging strategy for resolving sparse high-
                    Z
                    interfacial species. This work enables real-space, site-resolved adsorption-structure analysis that complements ensemble-averaged structural methods and provides a basis for mechanistic models of contaminant retention and structure-guided sorbent design.

title: A programmable cell-free biosensor device for on-demand detection of pathogens and antibiotics
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Cell-free systems provide a versatile platform for engineering customizable, gene circuit-based biosensors for decentralized, low-cost molecular diagnostics. Nevertheless, their performance in complex samples is often compromised by matrix interference, necessitating laborious preprocessing that restricts field deployment. Here, we developed a programmable, on-demand, cell-free kit (POCKit) that integrates sample pretreatment with point-of-care detection. The POCKit device comprises a negative pressure storage chamber and a sampling-sensing chamber, which can be connected to a microneedle array or pipette module for sample collection, filtration and target detection via a freeze-dried cell-free molecular reaction network. The POCKit enables detection of
                    Pseudomonas aeruginosa
                    infection in wound exudates, interstitial fluids and artificial sputum within one hour. It also detects tetracycline in food and environmental water, distinguishing tetracycline-spiked samples from negative controls without specialized equipment or tedious preparation. A portable fluorescence imaging box and smartphone application further support real-time signal acquisition and analysis, offering a ready-to-use platform for on-site diagnostics across biomedicine, food safety, and environmental monitoring.

title: DAS reveals continuous, multicore architecture of the Alpine Fault, New Zealand
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract: The Alpine Fault accommodates much of the relative motion between the Australian and Pacific plates in southern New Zealand and is expected to produce large earthquakes in coming decades. How slip evolves and what ground motions are produced during the next rupture are expected to depend strongly on the continuity of principal slip zones and overall fault width. Despite extensive study, the along-strike structure of the fault and its continuity across segment boundaries remain poorly constrained. Here, we use distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) along a 30-kilometer fiber-optic array crossing the Alpine Fault to record fault-zone guided waves (FZGWs) from local earthquakes. The FZGW observations, supported by numerical modeling and passive seismic imaging, reveal up to six narrow (∼10 meters) fault cores embedded within a 200-meter-wide low-velocity zone interpreted as the fault’s inner damage zone. The principal fault core feature persists for ∼180 kilometers along strike between the Central and South Westland segments, crossing a pronounced geometric and kinematic boundary. The inferred damage zone width is consistent with empirical scaling for large-displacement faults. These results demonstrate that DAS can resolve fault-zone architecture at previously inaccessible scales and bridge geological and geophysical inferences, providing constraints on fault continuity, slip localization, and the potential for multisegment rupture in mature plate-boundary systems.

title: Continuously aligned biomimetic sites in MXene membranes for rapid lithium extraction
source: AAAS: Science Advances: Table of Contents
abstract:
Efficient separation of lithium ions (Li
                    +
                    ) from magnesium ions (Mg
                    2+
                    ) remains a central challenge for direct lithium extraction from salt lake brines due to their similar physicochemical properties. Inspired by biological ion channels, biomimetic membranes have been explored to improve Li
                    +
                    /Mg
                    2+
                    separation. However, most biomimetic membranes focus primarily on introducing recognition sites while overlooking the structural features of biological channels, particularly the continuous arrangement of coordination sites that facilitates efficient ion transport. Here, inspired by the continuous carbonyl coordination structure of the KcsA ion channel, 4-formylbenzo-15-crown-5 ether was periodically grafted onto poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) chains and integrated with MXene nanosheets to construct two-dimensional interlayer channels with continuously aligned crown ether recognition sites. This architecture shifts Li
                    +
                    transport from random diffusion to successive site-to-site hopping, reducing the effective transport energy barrier. The resulting biomimetic MXene membrane achieves a Li
                    +
                    flux of 0.12 mol·m
                    −2
                    ·h
                    −1
                    with Li
                    +
                    /Mg
                    2+
                    selectivity of 109 and performs effectively across various salt lake brines.

title: Compound heterozygosity for I692del and V726A variants in MEFV leads to severe autoinflammation and elevated interleukin-18 (CHIVE-18)
source: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences: Keyword search for query
abstract:
We describe a severe
                    MEFV
                    -associated autoinflammatory disease, distinct from familial Mediterranean fever (FMF), and designate it CHIVE-18 syndrome (Compound Heterozygosity for I692del and V726A
                    MEFV
                    variants and Elevated IL-18). We present the clinical features and inflammatory signatures of 44 CHIVE-18 patients and 9 other patients with two
                    MEFV
                    variants including I692del. Clinical findings in CHIVE-18 patients often include transfusion-dependent anemia, arthritis, organomegaly, inflammatory bowel disease, failure to thrive, and less frequently cytokine storm, Amyloid A (AA) amyloidosis, and neutrophilic dermatoses. Serum total and free IL-18 levels in CHIVE-18 patients were markedly elevated compared to those of healthy controls, classical FMF patients, and compound heterozygotes for I692del and a pathogenic
                    MEFV
                    variant other than V726A and were comparable to the previously described levels of patients with pyogenic arthritis, pyoderma gangrenosum, and acne syndrome. Cultured U937 cells expressing the V726A/I692del double mutant exhibited significantly increased release of IL-1β, IL-18, and lactate dehydrogenase compared to the other FMF-associated mutants. Patients’ myeloid cells showed enhanced STAT1 phosphorylation after stimulation with IFNγ. Despite having undetectable serum IL-1β, a previously reported CHIVE-18 patient with autoimmune hepatitis had in situ staining of a liver biopsy that showed high expression of IL-1β, TNFα, and IL-18, which localized to CD68+ tissue macrophages. CHIVE-18 patients usually require an IL-1 inhibitor and sometimes combination therapy with another biologic to control disease activity. ABSTRACT

title: Chemical defects in semiconducting polymers and their impact on reproducibility and device performance
source: Nature Reviews Materials
abstract: Conjugated polymers are central to the field of organic electronics. The continuous drive to develop high-performance materials and explore alternative synthetic routes has led to unprecedented chemical versatility, allowing researchers to finely tune semiconducting polymer properties for specific applications. However, non-optimal polymerization conditions and/or limited differentiation between reacting monomers may facilitate side reactions, leading to the covalent incorporation of structural defects. Depending on their nature, these defects can perturb the electronic structure of conjugated polymers, causing varying degrees of deviation from the envisioned structure. As a result, structure–property relationships depend not only on molar mass, molar mass distribution and end groups but also on defect level. In this Perspective, we discuss these structural discrepancies and encourage researchers to critically evaluate the polymers they synthesize and study, recognizing structural variability as a potential driver of batch-to-batch inconsistency. We illustrate the origins of structural defects, outline strategies to limit or avoid them, and assess commonly used characterization techniques. Furthermore, we showcase the influence of structural irregularities on physicochemical and optoelectronic material properties, as well as device performance. Finally, we explore how structural defects can present opportunities, potentially offering new perspectives for materials design.

title: Dominant role of Southeast Asian emissions in anthropogenic increases in global tropospheric ozone and southward tropical growth, 2000–2019
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Widespread increases in tropospheric ozone (O3) have been reported over the past two decades, with changes in anthropogenic emissions, particularly in Asia, identified as an important driver. Here we use global model sensitivity simulations to quantify changes in global tropospheric O3 burden and associated radiative forcing (RF) attributable to anthropogenic emission changes from 2000 to 2019, and assess the contributions from different Asian regions. Changes in anthropogenic emissions increased the global tropospheric O3 burden by 12.0 ± 0.5 Tg and global mean RF by 0.030 ± 0.002 W m–2 under fixed 2015–2019 meteorological fields. The increase was larger during 2000–2010 than during 2010–2019 and occurred predominantly in the tropics. Southeast Asia was the largest regional contributor over 2000–2019, accounting for 5.7 ± 0.4 Tg of the simulated global tropospheric O3 burden increase and 0.020 ± 0.002 W m–2 of RF. During 2010–2019, the increase in tropospheric O3 burden attributable to anthropogenic emission changes was larger over 0–30°S than over 0–30°N, indicating a southward shift in the tropical response driven primarily by Southeast Asian emissions. East Asia shifted from a major positive contributor during 2000–2010 to a negative contributor during 2010–2019. These results highlight the increasing importance of anthropogenic emissions from tropical Asia in shaping the global distribution of tropospheric O3 and its climate forcing.

title: Tailorable deep eutectic solvents for sustainable lignocellulose refining: from platform design to value-added products
source: National Science Review Advance Access
abstract: Efficient utilization of renewable carbon requires lignocellulosic biorefineries that can deconstruct plant cell walls while preserving the value of cellulose, hemicellulose and lignin. Deep eutectic solvents (DESs), constructed from programmable hydrogen-bond acceptors and donors, have emerged as tunable media for lignocellulose processing. This review discusses recent progress in the rational design of DESs for lignocellulosic biorefineries, focusing on binary, ternary, hydrated, biphasic, catalytic and biocompatible systems. By regulating acidity/basicity, polarity, hydrogen-bonding ability, viscosity, water tolerance, active sites and phase behavior, DESs can selectively disrupt lignin-carbohydrate complexes, stabilize or functionalize the components, and direct the downstream transformation of the components toward bio-based chemicals and functional polymeric materials. Component-oriented valorization routes are summarized, including cellulose-derived functional materials and platform chemicals, lignin-derived aromatics and functional polymers, and hemicellulose-derived furan chemicals. Key barriers to industrial deployment are also critically examined, including high viscosity, mass-transfer limitations, solvent loss, energy-intensive recovery, feedstock heterogeneity, incomplete mechanistic understanding and insufficient techno-economic and life-cycle assessment. Future opportunities are highlighted in artificial-intelligence-guided DESs discovery, novel membrane and electrodialysis DES-recovery technologies, DES-compatible chemo-biocatalysis and closed-loop process integration. Tailorable DESs are expected to evolve from empirical solvent systems into predictive, recyclable and product-oriented platforms for sustainable production of bio-based chemicals, materials and fuels.

title: Learning beyond rigid manipulation with hybrid soft-rigid robots
source: Nature Communications
abstract: Rigid-soft robot hybrids promise to unite the precision and repeatability of rigid manipulators with the compliance and adaptability of soft structures. Yet, full-fledged rigid-soft manipulators remain largely unexplored, in part because the intelligence required to exploit this combination is still missing. Here, we introduce a hybrid robotic system obtained by the series interconnection of a rigid arm and a soft manipulator, and systematically examine its ability to perform both established and previously inaccessible manipulation tasks. We show that a tailored imitation learning algorithm–generally applicable to this class of hybrid systems–leverages the complementary roles of rigid precision and soft embodiment to acquire manipulation skills and generalize them in a single shot across task variations. As a result, the system matches or exceeds the performance of rigid robots in classical tasks such as stacking, while enabling qualitatively new behaviors, including grasping objects through narrow openings.

title: Tunable diffusive memristor arrays for neuromorphic temporal computing
source: Nature Materials
abstract: The dynamic behaviour of diffusive memristors enables bio-realistic emulation of artificial neurons and synapses, yet scaling from individual devices to neuromorphic systems remains challenging. Stochasticity in ionic motion and filament evolution limits both the uniformity and tunability of these devices, hindering reliable system-level implementation. Here we present a framework for tailoring the relaxation dynamics of diffusive memristors via intrinsic and extrinsic tuning. Percolation in a thin platinum interfacial layer and grain boundaries in a polycrystalline hafnium oxide matrix spatially confine active metal-ion migration; this guided transport substantially improves device uniformity. Purpose-designed programming protocols enable tuning of relaxation time over two orders of magnitude. A prototype hardware system integrating a 28 × 14 array of tailored diffusive memristors and a memristive system-on-chip implements the hierarchy-of-time-surfaces algorithm, achieving 91.14% recognition accuracy on a downsampled neuromorphic-MNIST dataset. These results demonstrate a scalable approach towards robust and energy-efficient neuromorphic hardware for next-generation artificial intelligence.

abstract: Linear, branched and heterotypic ubiquitin (Ub) chains regulate essential cellular processes, yet their structural and functional analysis remains limited by the difficulty of preparing defined, homogeneous samples. ABSTRACT

title: Toward a Visible‐Range Helicity Filter: Panchromatic Magnetic Circular Dichroism via 4f‐Orbital‐Based Charge Transfer in a Cerium(IV) Complex
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Magnetic circular dichroism (MCD)‐based light‐helicity filters provide a material‐based approach to controlling the helicity of light. However, helicity control across the entire visible spectrum using a single molecular species has not yet been demonstrated. Herein, we report a tetravalent cerium (Ce(IV)) complex exhibiting panchromatic MCD properties originating from 4f‐orbital‐based ligand‐to‐metal charge transfer (LMCT) transitions. A Ce(IV) complex containing four electron‐donating anionic diethyldithiocarbamate ligands was synthesized. This complex exhibits panchromatic light absorption with both positive (520–780 nm) and negative (380–520 nm) MCD signals. Relativistic time‐dependent density functional theory (TD‐DFT) calculations reveal that this panchromatic light absorption originates from multiple LMCT transitions. The strong spin‐orbit coupling (SOC) associated with the Ce(IV) 4f orbitals facilitates the mixing of singlet and triplet LMCT excited states, enabling panchromatic light absorption. The 4f‐orbital‐based transition properties also contribute to effective MCD signals governed by the Faraday
                    B
                    ‐term. These findings highlight the potential of panchromatic MCD in a Ce(IV) complex as a promising approach toward the development of visible‐range light‐helicity filters.

title: Anion‐Anchoring, Anti‐Swelling Polymer Interphase Enables Durable Lithium Metal Anodes in Localized High‐Concentration Electrolytes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Localized high‐concentration electrolytes (LHCEs) can improve the cycling stability of lithium metal batteries by promoting anion‐rich solvation structures that favor the formation of inorganic‐rich solid electrolyte interphases (SEIs). However, their favorable interfacial chemistry is not self‐sustaining because the native SEI is heterogeneous and prone to repeated rupture during Li plating/stripping, thus progressively depleting active Li and electrolyte. Polymeric artificial SEIs have emerged as a complementary strategy for interfacial stabilization, but their effectiveness in LHCEs is limited by an inherent conflict: the polar functional groups that coordinate ions also coordinate solvents, causing polymer swelling, dissolution, and disruption of anion‐rich solvation structures. Here, we develop an anion‐anchoring and anti‐swelling artificial SEI (AS–SEI) by integrating imidazolium cations with long aliphatic side chains. Imidazolium cations enable anion anchoring to sustain the LHCE‐favored anion‐rich environment at the interface, while long aliphatic chains provide anti‐swelling behavior that protects anchoring sites from competitive solvation. Consequently, AS‐SEI exhibits a high Young's modulus (5.0–10.5 GPa) and a high Li
                    +
                    transference number (0.94), while promoting the formation of LiF/Li
                    2
                    O‐rich SEIs. Li||Cu cells achieve 480 cycles with 99.5% average Coulombic efficiency, while Li||NCM811 cells deliver ∼900 cycles with 80% capacity retention (a nearly threefold improvement), with the strategy remaining effective across ether‐, ester‐, and sulfone‐based LHCEs.

title: Selective Gas‐Phase Photocatalytic Methane‐to‐Methanol Conversion Over Gallium Oxynitride With Molecular Oxygen as the Sole Oxidant
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Selective oxidation of methane to methanol using molecular oxygen remains challenging because methane activation is often accompanied by deep oxidation of the desired methanol product. Here we report a metal‐decorated, partially oxidized GaON/GaN photocatalyst for gas‐phase methane‐to‐methanol conversion using molecular oxygen as the oxidant. The optimized Ag/GaON/GaN catalyst delivers a methane oxidation rate of 2.6 mmol g
                    −
                    1
                    h
                    −
                    1
                    with ∼85% CH
                    4
                    ‐to‐CH
                    3
                    OH selectivity under O
                    2
                    . When untreated room air is used as the oxidant in a closed‐loop recirculating system, the catalyst maintains an activity of 1.0–1.3 mmol g
                    −
                    1
                    h
                    −
                    1
                    in a 50 h test, with comparable methanol selectivity. Complementary mechanistic experiments and DFT calculations support a mechanism in which partial surface oxidation promotes O
                    2
                    activation, while residual surface –NH species may moderate the resulting reactive intermediates through local H‐transfer processes, thereby suppressing methanol overoxidation. These results highlight partially oxidized oxynitride surfaces as a promising platform for selective methane upgrading under gas‐phase photocatalytic conditions.

title: Interfacial State‐Perturbed Triplet Energy Transfer in Dye‐Sensitized Upconversion Nanoparticles for Early HIV Diagnosis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Early diagnosis of HIV infection is pivotal for curbing AIDS progression and enabling timely therapeutic interventions. However, current immunoassays remain constrained by inadequate sensitivity for detecting trace levels of the HIV‐1 p24 antigen during the seroconversion window period. In this study, we discover that subtle perturbations in the interfacial binding state of a carboxylated near‐infrared dye, Cypate, on sub‐7 nm NaGdF
                    4
                    :Yb
                    3+
                    /Er
                    3+
                    upconversion nanoparticles (UCNPs) dramatically modulate triplet energy transfer (TET) efficiency, resulting in a remarkable upconversion luminescence (UCL) response with a signal‐to‐background ratio as high as 375. By leveraging this interfacial state‐perturbed TET as a signal transduction model, we further develop a TET‐sensitized UCL immunosorbent assay (TET‐ULISA) for HIV‐1 p24 antigen detection. In this platform, the target p24 triggers alkaline phosphatase (ALP) to generate phosphate ions, which competitively displace Cypate from the UCNP surface, disrupting TET and producing a dramatic UCL response. The resulting TET‐ULISA exhibits high sensitivity for p24 antigen with a limit of detection as low as 112 fg mL
                    −1
                    , representing an 860‐fold improvement over the corresponding ALP‐based method by employing the identical immunoassay steps, thus enabling early HIV diagnosis within the critical serological window period.

title: Programmable Skeletal Editing of Pyridines Into Regiodefined N‐Alkyl Pyrazoles
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract: N‐ Alkyl pyrazoles are common motifs in pharmaceuticals and agrochemicals, yet their preparation as single regioisomers is often hampered by poor regioselectivity in the direct alkylation of NH‐pyrazoles. Here we report a skeletal‐editing strategy that converts readily available pyridines into regiodefined N‐ alkyl pyrazoles through selective two‐carbon deletion. The N‐ substituent is installed before pyrazole formation and retained through amine‐mediated Zincke‐type ring opening, acid‐promoted cyclization, and retro‐Mannich extrusion of a two‐carbon enamine, fixing the pyrazole regiochemistry at the precursor stage. The sequence contracts the C 5 N pyridine framework into a C 3 N 2 pyrazole, transferring the ring nitrogen, three carbon atoms, and their substitution pattern directly onto the product. The method accommodates diverse pyridine scaffolds and N‐ alkyl groups and enables the skeletal remodeling of structurally complex molecules, transforming a problematic regioselective N‐ alkylation into a programmable precursor‐design strategy.

title: Overriding Polarity Mismatch in Radical Difunctionalization of 1,3‐Dienes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The difunctionalization of conjugated dienes poses a significant challenge in controlling regio‐ and stereoselectivity due to the presence of two conjugated double bonds. Conventional radical addition reactions adhere to the polarity‐matching principle, wherein nucleophilic alkyl radicals preferentially attack the electrophilic C4 position of electron‐deficient 1,3‐dienes. Consequently, the polarity‐mismatched C1‐selective addition has remained unexplored. Herein, we report a three‐component 1,4‐dicarbofunctionalization of electron‐deficient 1,3‐dienes with
                    α
                    ‐aminoalkyl radicals and alkyl bromides via dual nickel/photoredox catalysis. This protocol overcomes the inherent polarity‐mismatching effect, achieving unprecedented C1‐selective addition with complete 1,4‐regioselectivity and excellent
                    E
                    ‐stereoselectivity. The reaction provides efficient access to structurally diverse
                    β
                    ‐amino acid derivatives, featuring broad substrate compatibility and promising utility in the derivatization of complex molecules. Combined mechanistic investigations and DFT calculations reveal that both radical addition and C–C reductive elimination govern the regio‐ and stereoselectivity. Notably, a significant hyperconjugative interaction between the forming C–C bond and the carbonyl group of the 1,3‐diene in the transition state plays a pivotal role in directing the radical addition to the polarity‐mismatched C1 position.

title: An Artificial Phosphoinositide Phosphatase Inhibiting Pyroptosis Cascade for Sepsis Treatment
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Sepsis mortality remains largely driven by dysregulated pyroptosis, where gasdermin D (GSDMD) pores release lethal cytokines via phosphoinositide (PIP)‐mediated membrane recruitment. To disrupt this process, we engineer terbium‐doped ceria nanoparticles (TCNs) with sublattice‐induced oxygen vacancies and optimized Ce
                    3+
                    /Ce
                    4+
                    ratios, functioning as artificial phosphatases that achieve > 20‐fold enhanced dephosphorylation activity against the model substrate (
                    para
                    ‐nitrophenyl phosphate) versus pristine nanoparticles. Mechanistically, TCNs dephosphorylate PIPs at the plasma membrane, disrupting the canonical pyroptosis cascade by simultaneously interfering with inflammasome activation and the N‐terminal domain of GSDMD (GSDMD‐NT) oligomerization, ultimately inhibiting lytic pore formation. This
                    pan‐
                    PIP dephosphorylation approach overcomes the limitations of natural phosphatases by enabling efficient lipid dephosphorylation and preventing GSDMD membrane localization. In vitro and in vivo experiments demonstrate that TCNs significantly reduce pro‐inflammatory cytokine release and improve survival rates in a murine model of endotoxemic sepsis. This work establishes nanoparticle‐mediated PIP modulation as a potential strategy for sepsis immunotherapy, rebalancing immune homeostasis through precision pyroptosis attenuation.

title: Photocatalytic PVDF Degradation Coupled With Catalytic Targeted Li Replenishment Toward Low‐Energy Repair of Spent LiFePO4 Electrodes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Directly repair is recognized as a promising route for recycling spent lithium iron phosphate (LFP), but it is challenged by uneven Li supplementation and high energy input. Herein, we propose a photocatalytic strategy for PVDF degradation coupled with targeted Li replenishment toward low‐energy repair of spent LFP materials. Supported by theoretical analysis and in‐situ characterizations, TiO
                    2
                    can generate photogenerated electron–hole pairs synchronously under UV irradiation. The photogenerated holes promote the formation of •OH radicals, which abstract hydrogen atoms from the methylene units in PVDF, triggering the scission of polymer backbones and thus enabling the effective degradation of PVDF. Meanwhile, the photogenerated electrons accumulated on TiO
                    2
                    create a strong reductive microenvironment conducive to the reduction of Fe
                    3+
                    to Fe
                    2+
                    , which reduces the Li
                    +
                    migration barrier and facilitates lithium replenishment. The TiO
                    2
                    catalyst can incorporate into the material lattice as a favorable dopant to optimize the performances of as‐repaired LFP material. Specially, the repaired LFP material with 2.5 mol% TiO
                    2
                    delivers a high discharge capacity of 140.6 mAh g
                    −1
                    at 1 C with 99.8% capacity retention ratio after 100 cycles. Even at a high rate of 5 C, it maintains 98.3% capacity retention ratio over 1500 cycles.

title: Boosting DMF Electrosynthesis Over Bifunctional NiCo Catalysts via Methanol‐Supplemented *CHO Supply
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Traditional industrial routes for
                    N,N
                    ‐dimethylformamide (DMF) synthesis typically require harsh conditions of high temperature and pressure, leading to high energy consumption and a large carbon footprint. Electrosynthesis of DMF has emerged as a sustainable alternative; however, this pathway still faces the challenges of low activity and poor selectivity. In this study, we present an efficient bifunctional NiCo electrocatalyst synthesized via the electrodeposition method. This catalyst achieves a DMF Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 56% with a production rate of 518 µmol cm
                    −2
                    h
                    −1
                    . Combined in situ characterization and density functional theory (DFT) calculations reveal that NiOOH and CoOOH species act as potent oxygen‐transfer mediators, facilitating N–H bond activation and dehydrogenation of dimethylamine (DMA). These species also promote C–N coupling between the *N(CH
                    3
                    )
                    2
                    intermediate and *CHO intermediates derived from both methanol and the self‐decomposition of DMA. Furthermore, we find that the introduction of methanol provides a sufficient supply of *CHO intermediates, thereby further enhancing the selectivity of DMF synthesis compared with using DMA as the sole substrate. This work not only identifies the origin of the *CHO donor and its pivotal function in DMF electrosynthesis but also provides a foundation for designing multicomponent synergistic catalysts for advanced electrosynthesis.

title: Supramolecular Iron(II)‐Anchored Porphyrin Glycoassemblies Enable Galectin‐Targeted Photodynamic Therapy
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Photodynamic therapy (PDT) relies on photosensitizers that generate reactive oxygen species (ROS) upon light irradiation to trigger cytotoxic effects in target tissues. Porphyrins are among the most widely used PDT photosensitizers due to their strong visible‐light absorption and efficient ROS generation, although their broad application is limited by poor aqueous solubility, aggregation, and limited selectivity. Here, Fe(II)‐anchored porphyrin nanocages displaying peripheral lactose residues were prepared by coordination‐driven subcomponent self‐assembly to combine photodynamic activity with multivalent glycan presentation. The resulting cubic Fe
                    8
                    L
                    6
                    architectures were characterized by NMR spectroscopy, UV–vis spectroscopy, dynamic light scattering, and transmission electron microscopy. The zinc‐metalated porphyrin nanoassembly, [
                    1‐Zn
                    ][BF
                    4
                    ]
                    16
                    , generated both singlet oxygen and superoxide upon red‐light irradiation, providing access to multiple ROS pathways. Isothermal titration calorimetry revealed high‐affinity binding to galectin‐3 (
                    K
                    d
                     = 2.65 ± 0.26 µM), a lectin commonly upregulated in epithelial cancers. A549 cells treated with [
                    1‐Zn
                    ][BF
                    4
                    ]
                    16

                    1‐Zn
                    ][BF
                    4
                    ]
                    16
                    toxicity. These results demonstrate that coordination‐driven self‐assembly provides an effective strategy for integrating multivalent lectin recognition and photodynamic activity within a single nanoscale architecture.

title: Single‐Vesicle Membrane Order‐Resolved Super‐Resolution Imaging Reveals Cholesterol Enrichment and Its Functional Role in Extracellular Vesicle Uptake
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are heterogeneous in membrane composition, yet conventional lipid analysis cannot resolve individual vesicles. Here we develop membrane order‐resolved, spectrally encoded super‐resolution imaging to simultaneously quantify membrane order and size at the single‐EV level. Combining Nile Red single‐molecule spectroscopy with localization microscopy achieves ∼30 nm resolution and reveals pronounced vesicle‐to‐vesicle heterogeneity. Using defined liposomes, cholesterol enrichment, and pharmacological inhibition, we establish membrane order as a sensitive surrogate for relative cholesterol content in individual EVs. Application to EVs from breast, gastric, and oral cell lines reveals cell‐type‐ and tissue‐dependent differences. Most cancer‐cell‐derived EVs show higher membrane order and higher inferred cholesterol than non‐tumor counterparts, although MDA‐MB‐231 EVs are an exception. Functional assays demonstrate that increasing EV membrane cholesterol enhances cellular uptake and shifts internalization from clathrin‐mediated to non‐clathrin‐mediated pathways. These findings identify cholesterol enrichment as a frequent feature of cancer‐cell‐derived EVs and link membrane composition to uptake efficiency and pathway selection. This work provides a single‐EV analytical platform and new insight into how membrane lipid heterogeneity regulates EV‐mediated intercellular communication.

title: Revealing Oxidation‐State‐Dependent Selectivity in Urea Electrosynthesis Over Stabilized Co/CoOx Surfaces
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Electrocatalytic upgrading of CO

                    and nitrogen wastes offers a sustainable route for urea synthesis, yet its selectivity is limited by competing parallel reactions and operando catalyst reconstruction. Here, using cobalt‐based model catalysts, we demonstrate that product partitioning among competing pathways can be selectively directed by metallic and oxidized cobalt phases. By introducing oxophilic Cr
                    3+
                    to retard cathodic over‐reduction of cobalt oxides, we stabilize a non‐equilibrium Co/CoO
                    
                      x
                    
                    surface under working conditions. The optimized Co@CoO
                    
                      x

                    −1
                    g
                    cat

                    under pressurized CO

                    at −0.3 V vs. RHE. In situ spectroscopy and theoretical calculations support a proposed oxidation‐state‐dependent relay mechanism in which metallic Co favors CO
