title: Unlocking Intrinsic Narrowband Organic Ultralong Afterglow Through Efficient Two‐Photon Ionization
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Organic ultralong afterglow (OUA) materials are exclusively constrained by their reliance on host–guest exciplexes, which inherently suffer from spectral broadening and limited color tunability. Here we demonstrate an effective strategy to achieve narrowband OUA by harnessing localized excitons of guests through efficient two‐photon ionization (TPI). Through engineering multi‐resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‐TADF) guests, we achieve full‐color narrowband OUA emissions with full width at half maximum (FWHM) as narrow as 30 nm and unprecedentedly long durations exceeding 44 hours, which are comparable to commercial inorganic afterglow materials. The rigid planar molecular architecture of MR‐TADF not only promotes TPI but also reinforces host–guest interactions, thus fostering efficient charge separation to boost OUA properties. The intrinsic OUA can also be achieved based on fluorophore and metal–organic complex guests with planar molecular skeletons. The resultant materials enable promising applications in spectrally pure emergency afterglow lighting and sophisticated afterglow organic light‐emitting diodes (OLEDs). The afterglow OLEDs exhibit a maximum luminance of 26481 cd/m
                    2
                    , an external quantum efficiency of 8.7%, and record‐breaking ultralong electroluminescence afterglow lasting over 15 minutes. Our findings establish a valuable design principle for modulating charge migration and exciton transitions towards developing next‐generation OUA materials.

title: Built‐in Electric Field Modulating Interfacial Charge Dynamics in V2AlC‐Derived Magnetic‐Dielectric Heterostructures for Broadband Microwave Absorption
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The tailored design of magnetic‐dielectric heterostructures offers considerable potential for high‐performance electromagnetic wave absorption, yet achieving efficient interfacial charge separation remains challenging. Herein, we constructed VC/FeCoNi/Al
                    2
                    O
                    3
                    heterostructures with built‐in electric fields (BIEFs) via the topological structural transformation of V
                    2
                    AlC in Lewis acidic molten salts. This transformation involves the redox‐potential‐driven substitution by Fe/Co/Ni cations, leading to in situ alloying within the VC interlayers to balance the electromagnetic parameters. Theoretical calculations reveal that the work‐function difference drives directional interfacial charge redistribution, as evidenced by experimental observations of charge transfer and surface‐potential differences. This charge redistribution reconstructs the local electronic states, leading to interfacial orbital hybridization and establishing BIEFs at the heterointerfaces. Atomic vacancies and lattice distortions generated during etching, coupled with the BIEFs, enhance interfacial and defect‐induced polarization. Consequently, the optimized composite achieves a wide effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) of 6.72 GHz (at 1.7 mm) and a minimum reflection loss of −48.3 dB (at 2.8 mm). This BIEF‐mediated interfacial engineering strategy offers a viable route for designing high‐performance broadband microwave absorbers.

title: Molecular Crystal Phase Transformation via Nonclassical Pathways: Surfactant‐Based Kinetic Control of Metastable Amorphous Intermediates
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Molecular crystals serve as essential components in a wide range of functional products, yet their performance is often compromised by unpredictable phase transformations, particularly in aqueous environments. Although nonclassical, multistage pathways are frequently proposed for such transitions, the specific role of transient intermediates remains poorly understood. Here, we employ in situ atomic force microscopy and high‐resolution transmission electron microscopy to elucidate a nonclassical transformation pathway in the model molecular crystal piroxicam that proceeds via metastable intermediates. These intermediates serve as amorphous precursors that undergo densification prior to crystallization, facilitating a rapid transition from the anhydrate to a less soluble hydrate phase. The onset and kinetics of this transformation are tunable through the use of cationic surfactants with varying alkyl‐chain lengths. Longer‐chain surfactants cooperatively adsorb onto both dissolving crystal facets and nanodroplets in solution, creating a dense interfacial barrier that delays precursor formation and subsequent crystallization. This work presents a strategy to manipulate phase transformation pathways in molecular crystals by targeting the metastable intermediates via tailored additive‐interface interactions, enabling the predictive design of advanced materials with controlled phase behavior and enhanced performance reliability.

title: Tailoring the Na+ Transport Microenvironment With an Anion‐Capturing Interface Enables Low‐Temperature, Fast‐Charging Sodium‐Ion Batteries
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Na
                    +
                    desolvation and diffusion across the solid‐electrolyte interface (SEI) are two bottlenecks to fast charging at low temperatures in hard‐carbon sodium‐ion batteries. Here, we design an anion‐capturing interface that provides a customized interfacial environment to enhance interfacial dynamics at low temperatures. We demonstrate that phosphate can promote the formation of a homogeneous inorganic SEI by inducing anion enrichment near the inner Helmholtz plane. The phosphorus‐rich interface exhibits multiple benefits, including the formation of a built‐in electric field and a reduced energy barrier for Na
                    +
                    interphase diffusion. The hard carbon–phosphate interface (NP‐HC) anode maintains a capacity of 183.6 mAh g
                    −1
                    at 0.5 A g
                    −1
                    (−30°C). The pouch cell utilizing the NP‐HC anode achieves a 90.2% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at a 2 C rate. Even so, NP‐HC pouch cells can operate stably even at temperatures as low as −40°C, indicating their potential to enhance the performance of sodium‐ion batteries under harsh conditions.

title: A General Strategy to Identify Impurity‐Activated Room‐Temperature Phosphorescence in Synthetic Triarylamines
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Distinguishing intrinsic room‐temperature phosphorescence (RTP) from impurity‐derived emission remains challenging in organic luminescent materials, particularly when trace emissive species evade routine characterization. Herein, we establish a diagnostic framework for identifying impurity‐activated RTP in synthetic triarylamines through route‐, fraction‐, and purification‐dependent validation, impurity reconstitution, and theoretical analysis. Using TPA, TPAO, and related heteroatom‐engineered triarylamines as representative systems, we show that nominally identical samples can exhibit different RTP behaviors depending on synthetic history and purification extent, despite appearing chemically indistinguishable by conventional analyses. Progressive purification induces blue‐shifted and narrowed emissions and ultimately eliminates afterglow, revealing hidden emissive species. Structural analyses identify trace C–H arylation byproducts generated during metal‐catalyzed coupling reactions as a representative class of RTP‐active impurities. Reintroduction of independently synthesized impurity candidates into rigorously purified hosts restores phosphorescence, providing direct functional evidence that synthesis‐derived byproducts can activate RTP. Theoretical calculations further show that these impurities possess lower‐lying triplet states and act as triplet‐energy traps. Extension of the workflow to related synthetic triarylamines reproduces purification‐dependent RTP loss and impurity‐enabled recovery, supporting the applicability of this strategy across the triarylamine systems examined here and establishing synthetic history and purification as critical variables in assigning the origin of organic RTP.

title: Mechanochemically Accelerated Sharpless Asymmetric Dihydroxylation With Expanded Substrate Compatibility
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    The Sharpless asymmetric dihydroxylation is an established transformation in organic synthesis for the preparation of chiral vicinal diols. However, conventional biphasic solution‐based conditions (typically water/
                    t‐
                    BuOH) require long reaction times (up to ∼48 h) and large amounts of solvent. Moreover, they often exhibit limited substrate scope due to low solubility of the substrates and functional‐group incompatibility. Herein, we report the first mechanochemical protocol for the Sharpless asymmetric dihydroxylation, which affords the desired diols with excellent enantioselectivity, comparable to that of conventional methods. Notably, most substrates are fully converted within 30 min without the need for large quantities of solvent. Moreover, the mechanochemical conditions enable efficient reactions of substrates that are challenging to convert under solution‐based conditions, including poorly soluble, base‐sensitive, and catalyst‐coordinating compounds. The practical utility of this protocol is further demonstrated by the efficient dihydroxylation of an intermediate of a natural product and a gram‐scale synthesis.

title: Electrochemical PVC Recycling Unlocks Efficient Ring‐Closure Toward Amine‐Bearing Ketene Acetals as Novel Monomers for Poly(Amino Ester) Synthesis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  A paired electrochemical synthetic strategy for the upcycling of poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC) is reported, enabling simultaneous cathodic dechlorination of the polymer backbone and anodic formation of cyclic halo acetals (CHAs) as monomer precursors. The process channels liberated chloride into cyclic acetal structures, which are converted into cyclic ketene acetals and subsequently polymerized via radical ring‐opening polymerization (rROP) to access degradable polyester and poly(amino ester) materials. Electrochemical cyclization unlocks the synthesis of previously unavailable nitrogen‐containing cyclic ketene acetal monomers in remarkably high yields. Combined experimental and computational studies reveal a pronounced heteroatom effect on cyclization efficiency, attributed to conformational preorganization induced by an increasing gauche effect upon ether and amide incorporation. A nitrogen‐containing ketene acetal monomer was polymerized and copolymerized with established ketene acetals, affording new functional, biodegradable polymer materials. Successful copolymerization with methyl acrylate demonstrates the incorporation of hydrolysable moieties into otherwise persistent olefinic materials. Importantly, cathodic PVC dechlorination proceeds independently of the anodic transformation, highlighting the broad applicability of this paired‐electrolysis strategy in an undivided cell. Overall, this work establishes a versatile electrochemical PVC recycling process while simultaneously generating previously inaccessible monomer building blocks for biodegradable polymer synthesis.

title: Hofmeister Engineering Enables High‐Voltage Aqueous All‐Organic Batteries
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Aqueous all‐organic batteries (AOBs) offer a safe and sustainable alternative for electrochemical energy storage, yet their energy density is constrained by the limited availability of organic redox couples with high‐working voltages. Here we develop a versatile redox couple by pairing a 3,4,9,10‐perylenetetracarboxylic diimide (PTCDI) anode with a quaternary‐ammonium bromine cathode, enabling an initial discharge voltage of up to 2.0 V through reversible two‐electron bromine conversion (Br
                    −
                    /Br
                    0
                    /Br
                    +
                    ). This battery chemistry is compatible with diverse charge carriers, including Li
                    +
                    , Na
                    +
                    , K
                    +
                    , NH
                    4
                    +
                    , Ca
                    2+
                    , and Mg
                    2+
                    . We further reveal that electrolyte ions exert distinct effects on electrode reactions: Cations primarily regulate reaction kinetics, whereas anions govern both reversibility and kinetics through the Hofmeister effect. Kosmotropic anions suppress polybromide dissolution and improve reversibility, but retard electrode kinetics, while chaotropic anions facilitate reaction kinetics at the expense of active‐material retention. Guided by this mechanistic insight, a hybrid kosmotropic/chaotropic electrolyte balances these competing effects. The optimized one‐electron configuration retains 83.1% of its capacity after 12 000 cycles, while the two‐electron configuration delivers an energy density of approximately 107 Wh kg
                    −1
                    based on the combined electrode active‐material mass. High areal capacities exceeding 4 mAh cm
                    −2
                    further demonstrate its practical potential. This work establishes electrolyte solvation engineering as an effective strategy for high‐energy AOBs.

title: MitoDART: Mitochondria‐Targeted Intracellular DNA Assembly for Selective Mitochondrial Interference and Early Molecular Response Monitoring
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Rational modulation of mitochondrial functions to reprogram cellular behavior and fate has emerged as a promising therapeutic paradigm. However, it is still challenging to achieve cell‐selective mitochondrial interference with in situ monitoring of early molecular responses. In this study, we report a
                    mito
                    chondria‐targeted dual‐biomarker‐activated intracellular
                    D
                    NA
                    a
                    ssembly for mitochondrial
                    r
                    egulation and
                    t
                    racking (Mito‐DART), which enables cell‐selective interference of mitochondria and in situ biosensing for early assessment of molecular responses. Based on the AND logic responsive to two tumor biomarkers, apurinic/apyrimidinic endonuclease 1 (APE1) and microRNAs, Mito‐DART is specifically activated in tumor cells and undergoes hybridization chain reaction (HCR)‐driven DNA assembly, leading to mitochondrial dysfunction and apoptosis‐associated cellular responses. More importantly, Mito‐DART enables in situ monitoring of cytochrome c (Cyt c) release, an early molecular marker of mitochondria‐mediated apoptosis, within 1 h following mitochondrial disruption, providing an early molecular readout of mitochondria‐mediated apoptotic signaling that complements conventional tissue‐level endpoint assessments. Overall, this design provides a programmable framework for biomarker‐gated mitochondrial intervention that combines selective activation with built‐in assessment of downstream molecular responses.

title: Novel Fluorinated Amino‐Ester Electrolyte With Host–Guest Solvation Enables High‐Voltage and Thermally Safe Lithium–Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Lithium–metal batteries (LMBs) face critical bottlenecks to high energy density, long cycle life, and thermal safety, mainly due to insufficient oxidation stability and thermal tolerance of solvation structures in conventional carbonate/ether electrolytes. In this work, we develop a host–guest solvation structure via a molecular fluorination strategy based on a tertiary amine‐ester scaffold functionalized with trifluoroethyl (CF

                    CH
                    2
                    ─) and hexafluoroisopropyl ((CF
                    3

title: Hole Mobility Synchronizes Carbon Oxidation and Nitrate Reduction to Switch Photocatalytic Selectivity between Ammonia and Urea
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Photocatalytic conversion of nitrate and renewable carbon feedstocks offers a sustainable route to nitrogen chemicals but remains constrained by mismatched oxidation–reduction kinetics and inefficient C–N coupling. Here, we identify hole mobility as a decisive kinetic regulator that governs nitrate photoreduction selectivity by synchronizing carbon activation and nitrogen reduction pathways. By introducing cadmium vacancies into single‐atom Cu‐anchored CdS, we substantially reduce effective hole mass and accelerate hole transport, enabling oxidative C–C cleavage of biomass‐derived oxalic‐acid to generate reactive *COOH. Concurrently, hole mobility‐induced electron localization at Cu stabilizes nitrate‐derived *NH
                    2
                    , promoting selective *NH
                    2
                    ‐*COOH coupling while suppressing deep protonation to ammonia. Accordingly, Cu/CdS‐V
                    Cd
                    achieves a record urea yield of 1024 µmol g
                    −1
                    h
                    −1
                    with >99% selectivity, approximately fourteen times higher than state‐of‐the‐art nitrate‐based photocatalysts. In contrast, vacancy‐free Cu/CdS with low hole mobility fails to activate carbon feedstock and instead produces ammonia with >99% selectivity. In‐situ spectroscopy and density functional theory reveal that enhanced hole mobility accelerates oxalic‐acid oxidation, strengthens *NH
                    2
                    adsorption, and lowers the free‐energy barrier for C–N coupling to enable selective urea formation. These findings establish charge‐carrier mobility, rather than isolated active‐site activity, as a governing principle for artificial photosynthesis, offering a general strategy for selective multi‐reactant photocatalytic transformations.

title: Pulse‐Programmable Electrostatic Memory Using Ultrathin Hexagonal Boron Nitride
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Non‐volatile memory elements that enable multifunctionality and seamless integration with emerging quantum materials are of increasing interest for next‐generation electronic systems. In van der Waals heterostructures, hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) is widely employed as an inert substrate, encapsulation layer, and gate dielectric. Here we show that ultrathin (∼1.2 nm) hBN can also function as an active, pulse‐programmable electrostatic medium, enabling non‐volatile resistive memory with tunable resistance states in a multi‐terminal device architecture without dedicated gate or floating‐gate elements. Under millisecond current pulses, devices exhibit robust polarity‐dependent hysteresis in both transverse and longitudinal resistance, with programmed states exhibiting long retention times up to room temperature. The switching amplitude is strongly enhanced near the charge‐neutrality regime and vanishes in control devices without hBN, establishing ultrathin hBN as the essential functional element. We attribute this behavior to field‐assisted charge injection and trapping in hBN and near its interfaces, generating metastable electret‐like states that modify the local electrostatic potential landscape and thereby reconfigure electronic transport in the underlying channel. Our results identify few‐layer hBN as an active dielectric platform for non‐volatile memory and reveal a route toward electrostatically programmable transport functionalities in van der Waals systems.

title: Abrupt surface water decline during 2023–2024 record warming
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Global warming is expected to accelerate the hydrological cycle, yet its impact on terrestrial water availability is uncertain. Using assimilated streamflow observations from 150 major basins and satellite data for over 1.2 million water bodies, we show a global-scale synchronized decline of streamflow and surface water storage during the 2023–2024 record-warm period, the largest reduction since 1991. South America accounted for 70.4 ± 4.2% of the global streamflow decline. This abrupt depletion was driven by compound ocean–atmosphere forcing, in which concurrent El Niño and tropical North Atlantic warming triggered large-scale atmospheric subsidence, moisture divergence, and amplified drought. These findings reveal that extreme warming can induce abrupt water losses even in humid regions, underscoring a critical vulnerability of global hydrology and water security.

source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Much has been written about how the social contract between science and society in the United States is in crisis. According to its terms, research will yield broad economic, health, and security benefits to the very public that funds it. But this relationship depends on public trust in science, its systems, and the scientists themselves, and therein lies the problem. Beyond making discoveries and publishing results, scientists shape their own culture, and that is where some changes may be the key to rebuilding public trust.

title: Rough fracture zone as a gateway to the 2025 Mw 8.8 Kamchatka earthquake
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract:
Rough fault segments typically terminate giant earthquakes but are rarely reported to foster them. However, rupture characteristics of the 2025 moment magnitude (
                    M
                    w
                    ) 8.8 Kamchatka megathrust earthquake are consistent with initiation in a rough zone. Its early rupture was sluggish, lasting ~50 seconds with limited slip but strong, scattered high-frequency radiation. Rupture then propagated southward into a smoother segment, producing >20 meters slip with less intense high-frequency radiation. Using also the rupture characteristics of four
                    M
                    w
                    7+ foreshocks and aftershocks, we reveal variably sized seismic patches within the rough zone. We interpret these behaviors as manifestations of stress or frictional heterogeneities on the rough segment that favor localized failures yet can foster a giant rupture when spatially connected to a smooth, locked neighboring segment, a scenario previously underrecognized and meriting consideration in seismic hazard assessments.

title: Millisecond-scale imaging of fragmented earthquake rupture by near-source fiber-optic sensing
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract:
Small earthquakes [i.e., those of magnitude (
                    M
                    ) <3] are commonly modeled as simple circular ruptures, leaving the fine-scale spatial attributes of rupture dynamics unresolved. We used near-source distributed acoustic sensing to image the millisecond-scale rupture of an
                    M
                    2 earthquake within a swarm sequence in California’s Brawley Seismic Zone. Inverting fiber-derived apparent source time functions revealed two distinct rupture episodes separated by 42 milliseconds, reflecting rupture arrest followed by dynamic renucleation. Analysis of a 3-hour sequence showed adjacent, largely nonoverlapping fault patches activated in succession, forming complementary slip partitioning. These fragmented failure patterns within the
                    M
                    2 rupture and its sequence limited rupture growth, consistent with the absence of a dominant mainshock. Microearthquakes, which are now accessible by fiber-optic sensing, provide direct constraints on fault mechanics across scales bridging laboratory experiments and large earthquakes.

title: Integrating established and emerging tools to assess wildlife condition from the ground, up
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Metabolic energy links individual physiology to population-level dynamics, making wildlife body condition a cornerstone of conservation science. Emerging technologies, including unoccupied aircraft systems, make remote assessment of animal condition possible at unprecedented scales, and physiologically grounded validation is essential for strong inference. Here we examine the strengths and challenges of traditional and remote methods, using a comparative perspective that emphasizes both lipid and lean mass dynamics in evaluating wildlife health. We provide a framework that integrates complementary approaches to assess wildlife condition across diverse systems, matching emerging methods with the required physiological resolution, species characteristics, and temporal and spatial scales, while enhancing research ethics. Expanding capacity to track wildlife energetics from individuals to populations requires novel approaches and is vital for conservation in a changing world.

title: An engineered cohesion system reduces errors in aged mammalian eggs
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: In humans, female fertility declines rapidly from approximately 35 years onward owing to a steep increase in eggs in which chromosomes have split prematurely or that harbor an incorrect number of chromosomes (aneuploid eggs). A leading cause of age-related aneuploidy in eggs is the premature separation of sister chromatids (PSSC), which is caused by a loss of cohesin from chromosomes. In this study, we created an artificial cohesion system that reduces PSSC in aged mouse eggs. We further engineered a separase-cleavable sequence into the system, allowing for its scheduled deactivation during anaphase. We demonstrated that the artificial cohesion system could be adapted to tether human chromosomes, providing a proof of principle for the future development of approaches to reduce PSSC in eggs from women of advanced reproductive age.

title: Mitochondrial profiling links tumor genotype to metabolic and immune vulnerabilities in liver cancer
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Although oncogenic alterations influence tumor metabolism, how they impose distinct metabolic programs within a shared tissue remains poorly defined. We developed mitochondrial profiling platforms comparing metabolites and proteins in primary liver cancer (PLC) models. Analysis of six PLCs revealed that mitochondrial metabolism is dictated by oncogene identity. Kras-driven tumors required creatine metabolism to buffer energy, whereas c-MYC-driven tumors relied on oxidative phosphorylation. Among c-MYC-driven PLCs, Pten-deficient tumors accumulated mitochondrial phosphoethanolamine, a precursor of phosphatidylethanolamine (PE). Inhibition of PE synthesis selectively impaired Pten-deficient tumor growth and extended survival, partly through CD8+ T cell infiltration and sensitization to tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α-mediated cytotoxicity. Mechanistically, PE depletion increased the level of surface TNF receptors, promoting proinflammatory responses. These findings uncover genotype-specific metabolic liabilities and establish PE synthesis as a mechanism of immune evasion in PLC.

title: Counter-ion confinement reverses ion selectivity in subnanometer channels
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Ion transport in nano- and subnanometer channels is central to processes such as ion separation, energy conversion and storage, and nanofluidics. Conventionally, positively charged nanochannels favor anion transport and vice versa. We report that cationic covalent organic framework membranes with sub–one-nanometer channels exhibit selective cation transport. This reversal in selectivity arises from a counter-ion confinement effect, which inverts the electrostatic environment inside the channel wall and creates a secondary confinement region. The counter-ion confinement mechanism concomitantly suppresses coexisting ion competition in mixed-salt systems, enabling membranes to retain high selectivity under practical separation conditions. Our findings provide a design strategy for creating adaptive and highly selective membranes for precise ion transport and separation.

title: Priming of AGO2 by type I interferons balances inflammation and antiviral immunity
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Argonaute-2 (AGO2)–mediated RNA silencing contributes to antiviral defenses in plants and insects and may contribute to mammalian immunity, too. However, it is unknown whether AGO2 is modified upon infection or inflammation in mammals. We identified that the ubiquitin ligase RING-finger protein 126 (RNF126) interacts with and ubiquitinates AGO2 to enhance its small interfering RNA or microRNA loading. Using data from cells in vitro and mouse tissues, we propose that RNF126 is induced by type I interferon (IFN-I) signaling and promotes the ability of AGO2 to silence proinflammatory genes and inhibit viral replication. Lipid nanoparticle delivery of RNF126 mRNA to mice inhibited inflammation and viral replication. These findings identify cross-talk of IFN-based immune signaling and AGO2-mediated RNA silencing and suggest that the RNF126-AGO2 axis helps to balance inflammatory and antiviral immune protection.

title: Shared patterns of human milk composition link mammary gland function to infant growth
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: The mammary gland produces nutrient-rich human milk (HM), yet how mammary functional state shapes HM composition and infant outcomes remains poorly understood. We used HM multiomics, including metabolomics, proteomics, micronutrients, macronutrients, and HM oligosaccharides, across 1543 samples from three cohorts, including two randomized trials, as a noninvasive readout of mammary functional state. Trajectory modeling and multiomic integration showed that maternal supplementation improved recovery from early growth faltering and revealed a shared HM compositional axis linking maternal nutrition to infant growth. Machine learning, with Human Protein Atlas–informed proteomics, identified seven HM biomarkers reflecting variation across key mammary domains, indexing milk synthesis, barrier integrity, and immune-repair activity. Elevated valerylcarnitine and low pantothenic acid emerged as metabolic signals linking mammary functional state to infant growth.

title: Nutritional interventions’ impacts on human milk: Three trials in low-resource settings
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: Human milk (HM) composition is variable to support changing infant needs and is influenced by maternal diet and health. We harmonized HM data from three randomized trials in Burkina Faso (MISAME-III), Pakistan (Mumta-LW), and Tanzania (ELICIT) within the International Milk Composition (IMiC) Consortium to test how maternal nutrition affects HM composition. Balanced energy-protein (BEP) supplements or nicotinamide given to lactating mothers increased milk B vitamins, whereas macronutrients, oligosaccharides, bioactive proteins, and microbiome composition were physiologically buffered. Metabolomic and proteomic analyses revealed shifts in vitamin-related metabolites, triglyceride profiles, and intracellular protein representation. In a MISAME-III subset, maternal and infant blood showed concordant changes. Postnatal BEP improved infant growth only in the more undernourished cohort. Improved milk micronutrient quality across settings supports extending maternal supplementation into lactation.

title: Atomic functional site scaffolding in biopolymers with RFdiffusion3
source: AAAS: Science: Table of Contents
abstract: The catalytic and other sophisticated functions of biomolecules arise from the placement of many atoms in three-dimensional space. We describe a generative artificial intelligence method for biopolymers, RFdiffusion3 (RFD3), which uses free-atom diffusion to satisfy complex sets of atomic constraints more rapidly and accurately than previous methods across several challenges, from enzyme design to RNA structure design. We demonstrate experimentally the power of the RFD3 pipeline for enzyme design by designing de novo phosphotriesterases with a complex active-site architecture that incorporates a carbamylated lysine coordinating two metal ions and zinc proteases specific for the transthyretin protein involved in amyloid diseases; in both cases, we obtained active catalysts in zero-shot 96 construct design campaigns.

title: Covalent–Ionic Bonding Regulation Enables Chemo‐Mechanical Stabilization of High‐Voltage O3‐Type Sodium Layered Oxide Cathodes
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Ni–Fe–Mn‐based O3‐type layered oxides are attractive cathode materials for sodium‐ion batteries, but their high‐voltage operation suffers from the coupling between phase transitions and lattice oxygen instability. In this work, guided by hard and soft acids and bases (HSAB) theory, we propose a covalent–ionic dual‐pathway decoupling strategy to stabilize high‐voltage O3‐type layered cathodes. The incorporation of Mg, Ti, and F constructs a rigid architecture in which a covalent Ti─O framework reinforces the transition‐metal octahedral skeleton to suppress detrimental phase transitions, while localized Mg─F ionic coordination stabilizes lattice oxygen through localized electrostatic anchoring to mitigate irreversible oxygen release. Through multiscale structural and spectroscopic analyses, we verify that this bonding regulation suppresses the O3→P3→OP2 multiphase evolution and lattice oxygen escape. The modified cathode maintains 76.32% capacity retention over 400 cycles at 1 C and exhibits robust cyclability across −10°C to 50°C; the assembled full cells achieve a reversible capacity of 166.27 mAh g
                    −1
                    with an energy density of 330.22 Wh kg
                    −1
                    at 0.1 C, and an initial capacity of 143.74 mAh g
                    −1
                    with 72.06% retention after 500 cycles at 1 C. This work demonstrates a bonding‐regulation paradigm that decouples chemo‐mechanical degradation in high‐energy‐density layered oxide cathodes.

title: Synergistic Water‐Deficient Inner Helmholtz Plane and Asymmetric Dual‐Site Nonmetal Catalysts Enable Stable Ah‐Level Aqueous Zn–I2 Batteries at Elevated Temperatures
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    At elevated temperatures, intensified water‐induced side reactions and iodine dissolution severely hinder the development of aqueous zinc–iodine batteries. Herein, a marginally hydrophilic and conductive modification layer with a hexagonal layered structure is constructed to stabilize the anode interface. This approach establishes a water‐deficient inner Helmholtz plane and reduces the fraction of weak hydrogen bonds, thereby suppressing spontaneous Zn dissolution and water decomposition. Concurrently, interfacial electronic structure regulation increases the energy barrier for the hydrogen evolution reaction and promotes uniform Zn deposition along the Zn‐(002) crystal plane, effectively inhibiting dendrite growth. These effects are corroborated by theoretical calculations and in situ characterizations. Furthermore, asymmetric dual‐site nonmetal single‐atom–cluster structures are introduced into the cathode host to enhance iodine adsorption and accelerate conversion kinetics, thereby mitigating iodine dissolution. Benefiting from this synergistic design, the assembled coin‐type battery delivers a discharge capacity of 95 mAh g
                    −1
                    after 60 000 cycles at 8 A g
                    −1
                    . A sub‐ampere‐hour‐level plastic‐cased battery employing a high‐loading cathode with a theoretical areal‐capacity of 5.6 mAh cm
                    −2
                    further demonstrates strong practical potential by maintaining excellent cycling stability at 3 C and at 50°C. An Ah‐level pouch battery also exhibits stable operation at 50°C.

source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    All‐solid‐state lithium–sulfur batteries (ASSLSBs) offer high theoretical energy density, yet their practical viability is impeded by sluggish cathodic redox kinetics and uncontrolled anodic dendrite growth. Here, we address these challenges by a dual‐interface engineering strategy that exploits halogen anion migration to in situ construct phase‐separated localized electrochemical microreactors (LEMRs) at both electrodes. At the cathode, an in situ‐formed Li
                    6
                    PS
                    5
                    Cl/LiCl/Li
                    2
                    S‐LiI internal LEMR activates the S
                    2−
                    /S
                    n+
                    (
                    n
                    ≥1) multi‐electron redox reaction beyond the conventional S
                    2−
                    /S
                    0
                    redox reaction while maintaining structural integrity. Concurrently, at the Li anode, an interfacial LiCl/C@LiI/LiCl‐LiI anode LEMR confines Li plating/stripping within the LEMR to suppress lithium dendrites. This dual‐LEMR architecture enables the optimized cells to deliver a capacity retention of 86.3% after 450 cycles at 3.6 mAh cm
                    −2

                    −2

                    −2

title: Antigen‐Presenting Microrobots Program CAR‐T Cell Function
source: Wiley: Advanced Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Mechanical forces are emerging as key regulators of T‐cell function, yet how active motion‐ derived mechanical cues from artificial antigen‐presenting cells (aAPCs) influence T‐cell activation and fate remains largely unexplored. Here, we develop self‐propelled antigen‐presenting microrobots (CytoBots)—gas‐driven magnesium microparticles functionalized with anti‐CD3 and anti‐CD28 antibodies—that actively navigate suspension environments and mechanically engage T cells. Unlike immotile aAPCs, CytoBots generate motion‐dependent, force‐bearing stimulation that enhances T‐cell activation. Single‐cell force spectroscopy shows that CytoBots double receptor–ligand binding strength and extend bond lifetime threefold, supporting a role for motion‐enhanced mechanical interactions in T‐cell activation. CytoBot stimulation is associated with enhanced proximal T‐cell signaling, increased phosphorylation of AKT and mTOR, and metabolic changes characterized by elevated mitochondrial respiration and glycolysis‐associated activity. These responses accompany the enrichment of stem‐like and central memory T‐cell populations. In humanized tumor models, CytoBot‐expanded CAR‐T cells exhibit superior cytotoxicity, persistence, and antitumor efficacy. These findings establish microrobotic antigen‐presenting interfaces as a generalizable strategy for programming immune cell function through dynamic mechanotransduction, opening new opportunities for next‐generation cell therapies.

ABSTRACT

title: Low‐Temperature‐Locked Crystallization Enables Stress‐Relaxed Antimony Selenide Thin‐Film Solar Cells
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Absorber quality is critical to the performance of thin‐film photovoltaics, particularly for antimony selenide (Sb
                    2
                    Se
                    3
                    ). Due to its quasi‐one‐dimensional crystal structure, the migration, rearrangement, and orientation evolution of Sb
                    2
                    Se
                    3
                    chains play a pivotal role in determining crystallization and microstructural behavior. However, rapid heating (as with conventional thermal annealing) typically induces competitive chain orientation and nonuniform stress relaxation. This results in defect generation, orientational disorder, and complex crystallization pathways that severely constrain device performance. To address these issues, we propose a low‐temperature pretreatment to precisely regulate the crystallization kinetics of Sb
                    2
                    Se
                    3
                    absorbers. Low‐temperature pretreatment applied to amorphous Sb
                    2
                    Se
                    3
                    films prior to annealing effectively suppresses atomic diffusion and structural disordering, while preserving short‐range ordered chain segments as structural motifs for subsequent crystallization. During the subsequent annealing process, progressive stress relaxation facilitates chain reorientation and crystal reconstruction, thereby influencing local Sb‐Se compositional evolution, promoting grain growth, and enhancing preferential orientation. This progressive ‘low‐temperature‐locking stress‐relaxation‐oriented reconstruction’ process markedly reduces residual stress and defect density, while improving charge transport and suppressing non‐radiative carrier recombination. As a result, our pretreated device achieved a power conversion efficiency of 9.78%. This strategy offers a general route to fabricating high‐quality, low‐stress, low‐defect chalcogenide films for efficient and stable photovoltaics.

title: SEI Evolution on Siloxene Anodes in Solid and Liquid Electrolytes via an Ion‐Sieving/Electron‐Conducting Interfacial Layer
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Silicon anodes suffer from severe volume expansion and unstable solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), which limit their use in both liquid and solid‐state batteries. Here, a two‐dimensional siloxene‐based LP@SONS, is constructed by anchoring polypyrrole nanoparticles and lithiated‐Nafion onto siloxene nanosheets. This architecture combines electron‐conducting pathways with a Li
                    +
                    ‐selective ion‐sieving layer, homogenizing Li
                    +
                    flux, restricting anion/solvent penetration, and buffering strain. The stable and compositionally identical platform enables direct comparison of SEI evolution in liquid and solid electrolytes. In liquid cells, the SEI grows in a bulk‐permeated (3D) manner, whereas solid electrolytes confine growth to a planar solid–solid contact, yielding a LiF‐rich, planar‐confined (2D) SEI that passivates rapidly. Remarkably, LP@SONS promotes thinner, more uniform, LiF‐rich interphases in both systems. As a result, it delivers high reversible capacity, excellent rate capability, and long‐term cycling in liquid and solid‐state batteries, with only ∼5% thickness expansion after 100 cycles. This work clarifies how electrolyte contact geometry governs SEI dimensionality and offers an interfacial engineering strategy for high‐capacity anodes.

title: Single‐Atom Based Dual‐Metal‐Active‐Site Catalysts for N2 Conversion to Ammonia and Urea Synthesis: Geometric Coupling, Electronic Polarization, Reaction Partitioning, and Intermediate Steering
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    N
                    2
                    conversion is increasingly recognized not as a simple activation process of an inert molecule, but as a coupled reaction network that requires synchronized N
                    2
                    adsorption, electron/proton transfer, intermediate hydrogenation, C─N coupling, product release, and side‐reaction suppression. Single‐atom catalysts provide atomic precision, well‐defined coordination environments, and tunable electronic structures, but their isolated active centers often struggle to satisfy the multiple and sometimes conflicting requirements of complex N
                    2
                    conversion. Single‐atom‐based dual‐metal‐active‐site catalysts are therefore emerging as cooperative catalytic architectures that integrate an atomically dispersed metal single atom with a second metal site in the form of an isolated atom, cluster, or nanoparticle. This review establishes a structure‐function framework for understanding these catalysts, focusing on dual‐site adsorption geometry, asymmetric electronic polarization, bifunctional reaction partitioning, and intermediate‐specific stabilization. Recent advances in ammonia and urea synthesis are discussed to reveal how dual sites regulate N
                    2
                    activation, proton supply, intermediate evolution, and selective C─N bond formation. Particular attention is given to metal‐metal interactions, support‐mediated charge redistribution, hydrogen transfer, and pathway‐dependent intermediate binding. Finally, key challenges, including precise dual‐site construction, quantitative synergy identification, and practical compatibility, are highlighted to guide the rational design of next‐generation dual‐site catalysts for sustainable N
                    2
                    conversion.

title: Dark Horse Absorbers for Indoor Photovoltaics: Toward Cheaper, Safer, and More Stable Alternatives
source: Wiley: Advanced Energy Materials: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Indoor photovoltaics (PVs) have emerged as a promising solution for powering low‐power electronic and Internet of Things (IoT) devices by harvesting energy from artificial light sources. The development of low‐cost, non‐toxic, and stable absorber materials is central to enabling sustainable and scalable development of indoor PVs. Among various candidates, chalcogenide and kesterite absorbers such as Se, Sb
                    2
                    S
                    3
                    , Sb
                    2
                    (S,Se)
                    3
                    , GeS, Cu
                    2
                    ZnSnS
                    4
                    and Cu
                    2
                    ZnSn(S,Se)
                    4
                    have recently attracted attention due to their earth abundance, environmental benignity, and suitable optoelectronic properties for indoor light harvesting. This review provides a comprehensive overview of reported Indoor PV devices based on these absorber materials. Beyond comparing reported device performances, it critically examines the relationships between their fundamental optoelectronic properties, absorber processing, defect and interface engineering, device architecture, stability, sustainability, and demonstrated integration with IoT applications. Although research on these systems remains at an early stage, rapid progress has been achieved, highlighting their strong potential for next‐generation indoor energy harvesting. Finally, we outline key challenges and future research directions to guide the development of efficient, stable, and environmentally sustainable Indoor PVs for powering low‐power electronics and IoT devices.

title: Ring‐Retaining Polymerization of Vinylidenecyclopropanes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Commodity feedstock‐derived vinylidenecyclopropanes (VDCPs) are a new class of allenic monomers stereoelectronically intermediate between butatrienes and allenes. While their butatriene character drives the C5 ring‐opening polymerization (C5‐ROP), the complementary allene‐type polymerization mode remains elusive. Herein we report this new pathway for VDCPs. Organonickel catalysts with coordinating counterions enable C2 ring‐retaining polymerization (C2‐RRP), yielding pendant alkylidenecyclopropane moieties. Computations ascribe this reactivity to strain‐release alkene coordination, which further enables one‐pot diblock copolymerization with conventional allenes.

title: An Expandable Library of Solid Polymer Electrolytes for Lithium‐Metal Batteries
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Solid‐polymer‐electrolytes (SPEs) offer alternatives to next‐generation solid‐state lithium‐metal batteries, promising advantages in mechanical‐compliance, processability, cost‐effectiveness, and safety. While tremendous efforts have generated diverse SPEs since 1970s, SPE‐practicality remains limited by the trade‐offs among ion‐conductivity, high‐voltage stability, and Li
                    0
                    ‐electrolyte compatibility. Here, we establish the first SPE library covering 12 SPEs across five polymer families, which allows us to collect large datasets on chemistry, interfacial, and electrochemical properties that unveil their hidden connections. Correlation analysis of these descriptors reveals binding‐strength between polymer and Li
                    +
                    , subtle variations in polymer molecular structure, and solid‐electrolyte‐interphase composition as dictating factors. Also discovered is that the standard deviation of coulombic‐efficiency rather than its average value governs the battery cycling stability. The SPE library can be rapidly expanded through two structural engineering pathways: grafting diverse functional segments onto backbones and constructing compositionally‐complex SPEs. As a proof‐of‐concept, we fabricate several such SPEs and find improved high‐voltage stability through gradually increasing the complexity of the polymer matrices. A terpolymer‐based acrylates SPE exhibits outstanding Li
                    0
                    plating/stripping over 1800 h, stable cycling in LiCoO
                    2
                    ||Li battery with 100% capacity retention and an average coulombic‐efficiency of 99.91% ± 0.09% over 100 cycles. This work provides a transformative framework to design the future polymer materials.

title: Ferroelectric‐Field Gating Suppresses the Outward Migration of Active Oxygen Intermediates in Li‐Rich Cathodes
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Li‐rich layered oxides deliver high capacities through cation–anion co‐redox chemistry. During high‐voltage charging, however, peroxide/superoxide‐like O─O intermediates migrate down their concentration gradient from oxygen‐redox‐active regions toward particle surfaces, accumulating at the interface. This accumulation accelerates irreversible O
                    2
                    evolution and structural degradation, leading to low initial Coulombic efficiency and rapid capacity fading. Here, we construct a spontaneously polarized ferroelectric LiNbO
                    3
                    interfacial layer that generates a built‐in electric field to regulate oxygen redox in Li‐rich cathodes. This electric field suppresses concentration‐gradient‐driven migration and interfacial enrichment of charged active oxygen intermediates, limiting O
                    2
                    evolution and preserving a uniform surface‐to‐bulk distribution of oxygen electronic states at high delithiation. Consequently, the optimized cathode delivers 310 mAh g
                    −1
                    , an initial Coulombic efficiency of 99.97%, and 79% capacity retention after 500 cycles. Furthermore, this strategy enables Li‐metal pouch cells to achieve an energy density of 620 Wh kg
                    −1
                    and graphite‐based pouch cells to maintain stable operation over 2000 cycles. This work establishes ferroelectric‐field regulation as an effective strategy for stabilizing oxygen redox chemistry in Li‐rich cathodes.

title: Membrane‐Fusion Navigated Cell Membrane Anchoring Enhances Pyroptosis for Photoimmunotherapy
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Pyroptosis, a membrane disruptive and highly immunogenic form of programmed cell death, remains underexploited in cancer photoimmunotherapy due to the lack of general design principles beyond photosensitizer engineering. Here, we establish a membrane confined strategy that directly programs pyroptotic execution by targeting the plasma membrane as the primary reaction interface. A membrane fusogenic liposomal system enables precise anchoring of a caged perylene bisimides (PBI) onto the cell membrane, bypassing complex molecular modification. Upon light irradiation, PBI undergoes photocyclization to generate an active photosensitizer (CBI) and a protonic acid in situ. This dual output synergistically amplifies reactive oxygen species (ROS) production within a confined lipid environment, promoting lipid peroxidation, GPX4 downregulation, and membrane destabilization. Consequently, pyroptosis is efficiently triggered alongside ferroptosis, leading to enhanced tumor cell killing and immune activation both in vitro and in vivo. By shifting the design paradigm from molecular optimization to cell membrane control, this work reframes the plasma membrane from a passive barrier into an active reaction platform, providing a general and modular strategy for programmable pyroptosis‐based photoimmunotherapy.

title: Synergistic Ethylene Glycol Synthesis via Photocatalytic CO2 Reduction Coupled With CH3OH Oxidation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Paired photoredox catalysis enables co‐valorization of CO
                    2
                    and small molecules to high‐value chemicals via concurrent oxidation and reduction half‐reactions. However, most systems feature decoupled half‐reactions with no intrinsic substrate‐product interplay, merely utilizing electrons and holes separately, and failing to realize convergent chemical synthesis. Herein, we demonstrate a tandem photoredox‐photothermal catalytic system for efficient ethylene glycol (EG) synthesis, comprising (i) the photoredox catalysis of CO
                    2
                    reduction integrated with C─C coupling of methanol (CH
                    3
                    OH) to EG over Cu‐doped Zn
                    0.75
                    Cd
                    0.25
                    S catalysts, and (ii) the photothermal conversion of syngas to CH
                    3
                    OH over commercial CuZnAl catalysts. Of note, the CH
                    3
                    OH formed in situ via CO
                    2
                    reduction can feed into the pool of oxidation substrates, while the co‐generated syngas (ideal H
                    2
                    /CO ratio ≈ 2) is further converted to additional CH
                    3
                    OH and then recirculated as a supplemental oxidation substrate. Such a tandem catalytic design achieves high atom‐ and redox‐economy for EG synthesis, delivering an exceptional apparent quantum yield of 24.1%, outperforming those previously reported for CH
                    3
                    OH coupling to EG under an inert atmosphere. This work highlights the promise of orchestrating photoredox‐based closed‐loop catalytic architectures for value‐added C
                    2+
                    chemical synthesis with high efficiency and selectivity.

title: Desymmetrization of Acyclic meso‐1,3‐Diols by Cu─H‐Catalyzed Dehydrogenative Silylation
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    A nonenzymatic desymmetrization of acyclic
                    meso
                    ‐1,3‐diols by Si─O coupling with a hydrosilane is reported. The
                    C
                    
                      s
                    
                    ‐symmetric diols undergo enantioselective monosilylation with a Cu─H/(
                    R
                    ,
                    R
                    )‐Ph‐BPE catalyst system. The choice of hydrosilane was critical for suppressing undesired bissilylation, with a tertiary homobenzylic silane providing the best results. A series of simple alkyl‐substituted 1,3‐diols was converted into the corresponding silyl ethers with high enantiomeric ratios, with an unsubstituted methylene unit in the 2‐position identified as the most favorable scaffold for efficient and selective desymmetrization. Further modifications of the obtained enantioenriched products additionally emphasize the synthetic value of the reported methodology.

title: Beyond Lewis Acidity: Thiophilicity and Redox Stability as Design Principles for Sulphur‐Containing Polymerisation Catalysis
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Catalysts for the ring‐opening copolymerisation (ROCOP) of sulphur‐containing monomers are almost invariably inherited from all‐oxygen chemistry, where performance tracks the barrier of the rate‐determining propagation step. We show that this transfer fails. The activity of Cr(III), Co(III) and Zn(II) complexes of a common salicylimine scaffold cannot be explained by computationally tracking monomer insertions and metal activity is better predicted off‐cycle. A revised experimentally supported computational hypothesis implicates metal thiolates, generated by side‐reactions at the chain end, to deactivate the catalyst by either binding too tightly to or reducing the metal centre. The resulting computational descriptors, thiophilicity and redox stability, are distinct from Lewis acidity and chemical hardness, and predicted Al(III) to be competent. Al(III) catalysis delivers recyclable sulphur‐containing copolymers with a high apparent weight of M
                    n
                     = 238.6 kg/mol. This unlocks previously underexplored processing methods for these types of materials such as melt‐spinning and scCO
                    2
                    ‐foaming. Our results suggest new structure–activity design rules for sulphur‐containing polymerisation catalysis which are urgently required to obtain technologically useful materials.

title: Nitrogen‐Rich Covalent Organic Frameworks Enable Reversible Lithium Deposition in Anode‐Free Lithium Batteries
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  
                    Poor lithium reversibility and sluggish interfacial kinetics limit the areal capacity and rate capability of anode‐free lithium batteries. A nitrogen‐rich covalent organic framework (COF) as an interphase layer promotes uniform lithium deposition, enabling plating/stripping at 20 mAh/cm
                    2
                    in Li/Cu cells and anode‐free full‐cell operation at 4.1 mAh/cm
                    2
                    , as reported by Z. Ouyang, S. Zheng, S. Li, et al., Angewandte Chemie Novit 2 (2026): e70027.

title: Isolation of Open‐Shell Vinylidene Complexes of Iridium, Ruthenium, and Osmium
source: Wiley: Angewandte Chemie International Edition: Table of Contents
abstract:
ABSTRACT
                  Open‐shell vinylidene complexes are prone to undergo fast, ligand‐centered radical reactions. Herein, we describe the synthesis of paramagnetic Ir, Ru, and Os complexes with terminal N‐heterocyclic vinylidene ligands. Under inert conditions, these complexes remain stable over extended periods, allowing for isolation on a preparative scale and crystallographic analyses (for Ir and Ru). The results of computational investigations, EPR spectroscopic, and reactivity studies imply that the radical is largely localized on the vinylidene ligand.
